title.zh: 卷一百二十七 列傳第五十二 張源裴
title.raw: 卷一百二十七 列傳第五十二 張源裴 Volume 127 Biographies 52: Zhang. Yuan, Pei

sentences.zh: 張源裴

translations.literal: Zhang, Yuan, and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, Yuan, and Pei.

sentences.zh: ◎張源裴

translations.literal: ◎ Zhang, Yuan, and Pei.
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Zhang, Yuan, and Pei.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞，字嘉貞，本范陽舊姓，高祖子咤，仕隋終河東郡丞，遂家蒲州，為猗氏人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen, style name Jiazhen, originally bore the old surname of Fanyang. His ancestor Zhang Zha served the Sui and ended as assistant administrator of Hedong commandery; the family then settled in Puzhou and became natives of Yishi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen, whose style was Jiazhen, was descended from the old Fanyang clan. His forebear Zhang Zha had served the Sui and died as assistant administrator of Hedong commandery; the family then made its home in Puzhou and were counted among the people of Yishi.

sentences.zh: 以五經舉，補平鄉尉，坐事免。

translations.literal: He was recommended on the Five Classics examination, appointed Pingxiang district defender, and dismissed for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended on the Five Classics examination, he was appointed defender of Pingxiang district but was later dismissed after running afoul of the law.

sentences.zh: 長安中，御史張循憲使河東，事有未決，病之，問吏曰：「若頗知有佳客乎？」

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era, Censor Zhang Xunxian was sent to Hedong; when matters could not be settled he was troubled by it and asked his clerks, "Do any of you know a fine guest?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an period, Censor Zhang Xunxian was dispatched to Hedong. When he could not resolve certain matters, he grew vexed and asked his staff, "Do any of you know an exceptional man?"

sentences.zh: 吏以嘉貞對。

translations.literal: The clerk named Jiazhen in reply.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk answered with Jiazhen's name.

sentences.zh: 循憲召見，咨以事。

translations.literal: Xunxian summoned him and consulted him on the affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xunxian summoned him and put the unresolved matters before him.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞條析理分，莫不洗然。

translations.literal: Jiazhen analyzed the principles point by point, each becoming perfectly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen laid out each point of principle in order until everything stood perfectly clear.

sentences.zh: 循憲大驚，試命草奏，皆意所未及；

translations.literal: Xunxian was greatly startled; he had him draft a memorial, and all went beyond what he had expected;
translations.idiomatic: Xunxian was astonished and had him draft a memorial; the result exceeded everything he had anticipated;

sentences.zh: 它日，武後以為能，循憲對皆嘉貞所為，因請以官讓。

translations.literal: Another day, Empress Wu considered him capable; Xunxian reported that everything was Jiazhen's work, and therefore asked to yield his office to him.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion Empress Wu judged him capable. Xunxian reported that his own answers had all been Jiazhen's work and asked to yield his post to him.

sentences.zh: 後曰：「朕寧無一官自進賢邪？」

translations.literal: The Empress said, "Would I rather lack an office than advance a worthy man myself?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "Would I rather go without an office than fail to advance a worthy man myself?"

sentences.zh: 召嘉貞見內殿；

translations.literal: She summoned Jiazhen to the inner palace;
translations.idiomatic: She summoned Jiazhen to the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 以簾自鄣。

translations.literal: she screened herself with a curtain.
translations.idiomatic: and screened herself behind a curtain.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞儀止秀偉，奏對偘偘，後異之。

translations.literal: Jiazhen's bearing was handsome and imposing; in audience he spoke boldly and clearly, and the Empress was struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen's bearing was handsome and imposing, and in audience he spoke with bold clarity. The Empress was struck by him.

sentences.zh: 因請曰：「臣草茅之人，未睹朝廷儀，陛下過聽，引對禁近。

translations.literal: He therefore requested, "I am but a man of the thatch hut and have never witnessed court ceremony. Your Majesty has over-listened to me and drawn me near within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore said, "I am only a man from the thatched hut and have never witnessed court ceremony. Your Majesty has been too generous in summoning me to audience within the forbidden precinct.

sentences.zh: 今天威咫尺，若隔雲霧，恐君臣之道有未盡也。」

translations.literal: Today the imperial majesty is but a foot away, yet separated as if by clouds and mist; I fear the way of ruler and minister is not yet complete."
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Majesty's majesty is but a foot away, yet separated as if by clouds and mist. I fear the bond between ruler and minister is not yet complete."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Empress said, "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 詔上簾，引拜監察御史，擢循憲司勛郎中，酬其得人。

translations.literal: She ordered the curtain raised, received him with a bow, and appointed him investigating censor; she promoted Xunxian to director of the Bureau of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, rewarding him for finding the right man.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the curtain raised, received him with a bow, and appointed him investigating censor. She promoted Xunxian to director of the Bureau of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, rewarding him for discovering the right man.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 時功狀盈幾，郎吏不能決，嘉貞為詳處，不閱旬，廷無稽牒。

translations.literal: At the time merit records piled up by the bundle and the bureau clerks could not settle them; Jiazhen disposed of them in detail, and within less than ten days the court had no backlog of documents.
translations.idiomatic: At the time merit records piled up by the bundle and the bureau clerks could not settle them. Jiazhen disposed of them in detail, and within less than ten days the court had no backlog of documents.

sentences.zh: 進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace secretariat draftee.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to draftee of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 歷梁秦二州都督、並州長史，政以嚴辦，吏下畏之。

translations.literal: He served in turn as military commissioner of Liang and Qin provinces and as prefectural secretary of Bingzhou; his government was conducted with strict efficiency and subordinate officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as military commissioner of Liang and Qin and as prefectural secretary of Bingzhou, governing with strict efficiency so that subordinates feared him.

sentences.zh: 奏事京師，玄宗善其政，數慰勞。

translations.literal: When he reported at the capital, Xuanzong approved of his administration and repeatedly comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported at the capital, Xuanzong approved of his administration and repeatedly comforted and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞自陳：「少孤，與弟嘉佑相恃以長，今為鄯州別駕，願內徙，使少相近，冀盡力報，死無恨。」

translations.literal: Jiazhen stated on his own behalf: "I was orphaned young and, with my younger brother Jiayou, relied on each other as we grew up; he is now vice prefect of Binzhou. I beg he be moved inward so that we two might draw somewhat nearer, that I may exert myself to repay you, and die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen spoke on his own behalf: "I was orphaned young and grew up relying on my younger brother Jiayou. He is now vice prefect of Binzhou. I beg that he be moved inward so we may draw somewhat nearer, that I may serve you with all my strength and die without regret."

sentences.zh: 帝為徙嘉祐忻州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore moved Jiayou to be prefect of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor moved Jiayou to be prefect of Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 突厥九姓新內屬，雜處太原北，嘉貞請置天兵軍綏護其眾，即以為天兵使。

translations.literal: The nine surnames of the Turks had newly submitted inward and were scattered north of Taiyuan; Jiazhen requested establishment of the Tianbing Army to guard and protect the multitude, and he himself was made Tianbing commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The nine Turkic clans had newly submitted and were settled north of Taiyuan. Jiazhen requested the establishment of the Tianbing Army to protect them and was himself appointed Tianbing commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年入朝，或告其反，按無狀，帝令坐告者。

translations.literal: The next year he came to court; someone reported he was rebelling; investigation found nothing; the Emperor had the accuser seated [for punishment].
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court. Someone accused him of rebellion, but investigation found no basis for the charge, and the Emperor ordered the accuser seated for punishment.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞辭曰：「國之重兵利器皆在邊，今告者一不當即罪之，臣恐塞言路，且為未來之患。

translations.literal: Jiazhen declined, saying: "The state's weighty armies and sharp weapons all lie on the borders. If today one who reports is incorrect and we immediately punish him, I fear we will block the path of speech and create trouble for the future as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen declined, saying, "The state's weighty armies and sharp weapons all lie on the borders. If today one who reports falsely is immediately punished, I fear we will block the path of speech and create trouble for the future as well.

sentences.zh: 昔天子聽政於上，瞍賦，蒙誦，百工諫，庶人謗，今將坐之，則後無繇聞天下事。」

translations.literal: In olden days the Son of Heaven heard government above; the blind chanted, the blind recited, artisans remonstrated, the common people slandered—now if we sit him for punishment, later there will be no way to hear affairs under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the Son of Heaven heard government above while the blind chanted, the blind recited, artisans remonstrated, and commoners slandered. If we punish him now, later there will be no way to hear affairs under Heaven."

sentences.zh: 遂得減死。

translations.literal: The accuser was therefore allowed commutation to lesser death.
translations.idiomatic: The accuser was therefore allowed commutation to a lesser punishment.

sentences.zh: 天子以為忠，且許以相。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven considered him loyal and moreover promised him the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven considered him loyal and moreover promised him the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞因曰：「昔馬周起徒步，謁人主，血氣方壯，太宗用之，能盡其才，甫五十而沒。

translations.literal: Jiazhen therefore said: "In the past Ma Zhou rose from the common road and, visiting the ruler when his blood and qi were still vigorous, Taizong employed him and could exhaust his talents; he had barely reached fifty when he died.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen therefore said, "In the past Ma Zhou rose from the common road and, when his blood and vigor were still at their height, visited the ruler. Taizong employed him and could exhaust his talents, yet he had barely reached fifty when he died.

sentences.zh: 向使用少晚，則無及已。

translations.literal: Had he been used a little later, nothing would have come of it.
translations.idiomatic: Had he been used even a little later, nothing would have come of it.

sentences.zh: 陛下不以臣不肖，必用之，要及其時，後衰無能為也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not consider me unworthy and will certainly use me, you must catch the right moment; when I am old and feeble I can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not consider me unworthy and will certainly use me, you must catch the right moment. When I grow old and feeble, I can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 且百年壽孰為至者？

translations.literal: And of a hundred years of life, who reaches the fullest?
translations.idiomatic: And of a hundred years of life, who reaches the fullest span?

sentences.zh: 臣常恐先朝露死溝壑，誠得效萬一，無負陛下足矣！」

translations.literal: I have often feared I might expire first like the morning dew in ditch and gully; if I can serve even in the slightest, that will be enough not to fail Your Majesty!"
translations.idiomatic: I have often feared I might expire first like morning dew in ditch and gully. If I can serve even in the slightest, that will be enough not to fail Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「第往，行召卿。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Go for now; when the time comes I shall summon you."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Go for now. When the time comes I shall summon you."

sentences.zh: 及宋璟等罷，帝欲果用嘉貞，而忘其名。

translations.literal: When Song Jing and others were dismissed, the Emperor wished finally to employ Jiazhen but forgot his name.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jing and others were dismissed, the Emperor wished at last to employ Jiazhen but had forgotten his name.

sentences.zh: 夜詔中書侍郎韋抗曰：「朕嘗記其風操，而今為北方大將，張姓而復名，卿為我思之。」

translations.literal: At night he summoned Palace Secretariat Vice Director Wei Kang and said: "I recall his manner; today he is a great general of the north, surname Zhang and a repeated given name—think of him for me."
translations.idiomatic: At night he summoned Palace Secretariat Vice Director Wei Kang and said, "I recall his manner. Today he is a great general of the north, surname Zhang with a repeated given name. Think of him for me."

sentences.zh: 抗曰：「非張齊丘乎？

translations.literal: Kang said, "Is it not Zhang Qiqiu?
translations.idiomatic: Kang said, "Is it not Zhang Qiqiu?

sentences.zh: 今為朔方節度使。」

translations.literal: He is now military commissioner of Shuofang."
translations.idiomatic: He is now military commissioner of Shuofang."

sentences.zh: 帝即使作詔以為相。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately had a draft made appointing him chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately had a draft made appointing him chancellor.

sentences.zh: 夜且半，因閱大臣表疏，舉一則嘉貞所獻，遂得其名，即以為中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Past midnight he was reviewing memorials of great ministers; lifting one, he found it submitted by Jiazhen, and thus got his name; he was at once made Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate Commissioner with same authority as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Past midnight, while reviewing memorials of great ministers, he lifted one submitted by Jiazhen and thus learned his name. He was at once made Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate Commissioner with the same authority as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居位三年，善傅奏，敏於裁遣。

translations.literal: He held office three years, skilled at presenting memorials and quick in disposing of matters.
translations.idiomatic: He held office three years, skilled at presenting memorials and quick in disposing of affairs.

sentences.zh: 然強躁，論者恨其不裕。

translations.literal: Yet he was forceful and impatient; critics resented his lack of generosity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was forceful and impatient, and critics resented his lack of magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 帝數幸東都，洛陽主簿王鈞者，為嘉貞繕第，會以贓聞，有詔杖之朝堂。

translations.literal: The Emperor repeatedly visited the eastern capital; Luoyang chief recorder Wang Jun built a residence for Jiazhen; when corruption came to light there was an edict to cane him in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor repeatedly visited the eastern capital. Luoyang chief recorder Wang Jun had built a residence for Jiazhen, and when corruption came to light an edict ordered him caned in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞畏蔑染，促有司速斃以滅言。

translations.literal: Jiazhen feared being tainted by contempt and urged the offices to execute him quickly to silence talk.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen feared being tainted by contempt and urged the offices to execute Wang quickly to silence talk.

sentences.zh: 秘書監姜交得罪，嘉貞希權幸意，請加詔杖，已而交死。

translations.literal: Palace Library Director Jiang Jiao offended; Jiazhen, coveting favor, asked that an edict also cane him; soon after Jiao died.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Library Director Jiang Jiao offended the court. Jiazhen, coveting favor, asked that an edict cane him as well, and soon after Jiao died.

sentences.zh: 會廣州都督裴伷先抵罪，帝問法如何，嘉貞復援交比，張說曰：「不然，刑不上大夫，以近君也。

translations.literal: When Guangzhou military commissioner Pei Xianxian ran afoul of the law, the Emperor asked what the penalty should be; Jiazhen again cited Jiao by analogy; Zhang Yue said: "That will not do—punishment does not reach up to grandees, because they are near the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou military commissioner Pei Xianxian ran afoul of the law, the Emperor asked what penalty should apply. Jiazhen again cited Jiao by analogy. Zhang Yue said, "That will not do. Punishment does not reach up to grandees, because they stand near the ruler.

sentences.zh: 士可殺不可辱。

translations.literal: A gentleman may be killed but not insulted.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman may be killed but not insulted.

sentences.zh: 向交得罪，官三品，且有功，若罪應死，即殺，獨不宜廷辱，以卒伍待也。

translations.literal: Formerly when Jiao offended, his office was third rank and he had merit; if the crime deserved death, then kill him, but alone we should not insult him in court, treating him like a common soldier.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiao offended before, his office was third rank and he had merit. If the crime deserved death, then kill him, but he should not be insulted in court and treated like a common soldier.

sentences.zh: 況勸貴在八議乎？

translations.literal: How much more when urging wealth and nobility fall under the eight deliberations?
translations.idiomatic: How much more when men of wealth and rank fall under the eight deliberations?

sentences.zh: 事往不可咎，伷先豈容復濫哉？」

translations.literal: What is past cannot be blamed; can Xianxian be maltreated again without cause?"
translations.idiomatic: What is past cannot be blamed. Can Xianxian be maltreated again without cause?"

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞退，不悅曰：「言太切。」

translations.literal: Jiazhen withdrew, displeased, and said, "Your words were too cutting."
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen withdrew, displeased, and said, "Your words were too cutting."

sentences.zh: 說曰：「宰相，時來則為，非可長保。

translations.literal: Yue said, "Chancellor—a post for the moment; one cannot hold it forever.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The chancellorship is a post for the moment. One cannot hold it forever.

sentences.zh: 若貴臣盡杖，正恐吾輩及之，渠不為天下士君子地乎？」

translations.literal: If eminent ministers are all caned, I fear we too will come to it—will you not leave ground for the gentry and scholars of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: If eminent ministers are all caned, I fear we too will come to it. Will you not leave standing room for the gentry and scholars of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 初，嘉貞在兵部，而說已為侍郎。

translations.literal: At first, when Jiazhen was in the Ministry of War, Yue was already vice director.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Jiazhen was in the Ministry of War, Yue was already vice director.

sentences.zh: 及皆相，說位其下，議論無所讓，故說不平。

translations.literal: When both were chancellors, Yue's rank was below him yet in discussion he yielded nothing; hence Yue was discontent.
translations.idiomatic: When both became chancellors, Yue ranked below him yet yielded nothing in debate, and so Yue was discontent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，嘉佑拜金吾將軍，兄弟要近，人頗憚冒。

translations.literal: Before long Jiayou was appointed General of the Golden Unbending Guard; the brothers being so close to power, people were much wary of presumption.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiayou was appointed General of the Golden Unbending Guard. With the brothers so close to power, people were much wary of presumption.

sentences.zh: 帝幸太原，嘉佑以贓聞，說訹嘉貞素服待罪，不謁，遂出為豳州刺史，說代其處。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited Taiyuan, Jiayou's corruption came to light; Yue urged Jiazhen to wait in plain dress for punishment and not attend audience; he was therefore sent out as prefect of Binzhou, and Yue replaced him in the post.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor visited Taiyuan, Jiayou's corruption came to light. Yue urged Jiazhen to wait in plain dress for punishment and not attend audience. Jiazhen was sent out as prefect of Binzhou, and Yue replaced him in the post.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞銜悔，謂人曰：「中書令幸二員，何相迫邪？」

translations.literal: Jiazhen nursed resentment and said to people, "There are luckily two directors of the secretariat—why press each other so?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen nursed resentment and said to others, "There are luckily two directors of the secretariat. Why press each other so?"

sentences.zh: 逾年，為戶部尚書、益州長史，判都督事，詔宴中書省，與宰相會。

translations.literal: After a year he was Minister of Revenue and prefectural secretary of Yizhou with concurrent supervision of the military commission; an edict banqueted him at the Secretariat together with the chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was made Minister of Revenue and prefectural secretary of Yizhou with concurrent supervision of the military commission. An edict banqueted him at the Secretariat together with the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞銜說不已，於坐慢罵說，源乾曜、王盩共平解，乃得去。

translations.literal: Jiazhen still bore a grudge against Yue and at the seat openly reviled him; Yuan Qianyao and Wang Tan together smoothed the matter, and only then could he leave.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen still bore a grudge against Yue and at the banquet openly reviled him. Yuan Qianyao and Wang Tan together smoothed the matter, and only then could he leave.

sentences.zh: 明年，王守一死，坐與厚善，貶臺州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Shouyi died; for being on close terms with him Jiazhen was demoted to prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Wang Shouyi died. For being on close terms with him, Jiazhen was demoted to prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 俄拜工部尚書，為定州刺史，知北平軍事，封河東侯。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Works, made prefect of Dingzhou with supervision of Beiping military affairs, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed Minister of Works, made prefect of Dingzhou with supervision of Beiping military affairs, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 及行，帝賦詩，詔百官祖道上東門。

translations.literal: On his departure the Emperor composed a poem and ordered all officials to escort him to the Shangdong Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On his departure the Emperor composed a poem and ordered all officials to escort him to the Shangdong Gate.

sentences.zh: 久之，以疾丐還東都，詔醫馳驛護視。

translations.literal: After a long while, on grounds of illness he begged to return to the eastern capital; an edict sent physicians by relay post to tend him.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while, on grounds of illness he begged to return to the eastern capital. An edict sent physicians by relay post to tend him.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四，贈益州大都督，謚曰恭肅。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-four; posthumously made Grand Protector of Yizhou, posthumous title Gongsu [Reverent and Solemn].
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four. He was posthumously made Grand Protector of Yizhou with the posthumous title Gongsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞性簡疏，與人不疑，內曠如也，或時以此失。

translations.literal: Jiazhen's nature was easy and undemanding, without suspicion toward others, inwardly open and free, yet at times lost ground because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Jiazhen's nature was easy and undemanding. He was without suspicion toward others and inwardly open and free, yet at times lost ground because of this.

sentences.zh: 有嗜進者，汲引之，能以恩終始。

translations.literal: Where there were men eager to advance, he drew them up and could treat them with kindness from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Where there were men eager to advance, he drew them up and could treat them with kindness from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 所薦中書舍人苗延嗣、呂太一，考功員外郎員嘉靜，殿中侍御史崔訓，皆位清要，日與議政事。

translations.literal: Those he recommended—Palace Secretariat draftee Miao Yansi, Lü Taiyi, evaluation-section vice director Yuan Jiajing, palace attendant Cui Xun—all held pure and important posts and daily discussed government affairs with him.
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended—Palace Secretariat draftees Miao Yansi and Lü Taiyi, evaluation-section vice director Yuan Jiajing, and palace attendant Cui Xun—all held pure and important posts and daily discussed government affairs with him.

sentences.zh: 故當時語曰：「令君四俊，苗、呂、崔、員。」

translations.literal: Hence the saying of the time: "Our Lord's four outstanding men: Miao, Lü, Cui, Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying of the time: "Our Lord's four outstanding men: Miao, Lü, Cui, and Yuan."

sentences.zh: 其始為中書舍人，崔湜輕之，後與議事，正出其上。

translations.literal: At first when he was Palace Secretariat draftee, Cui Shi looked down on him; later when they discussed affairs together, he would regularly be above Shi.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when he was a Palace Secretariat draftee, Cui Shi looked down on him. Later, when they discussed affairs together, he would regularly speak above Shi.

sentences.zh: 湜驚曰：「此終其坐。」

translations.literal: Shi said in amazement, "This man will end in that seat."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said in amazement, "This man will end in that seat."

sentences.zh: 後十年而為中書令。

translations.literal: Ten years later he became Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he became Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘉貞雖貴，不立田園。

translations.literal: Though Jiazhen was noble, he did not establish fields and estates.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiazhen had risen high, he did not establish fields and estates.

sentences.zh: 有勸之者，答曰：「吾嘗相國矣，未死，豈有饑寒憂？

translations.literal: When some urged him, he answered: "I have been chancellor of the state; while I am not dead, how could there be hunger and cold to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: When some urged him, he answered, "I have been chancellor of the state. While I am not dead, how could there be hunger and cold to worry about?

sentences.zh: 若以譴去，雖富田產，猶不能有也。

translations.literal: If by reprimand I am removed, even with rich fields and property I still cannot keep them.
translations.idiomatic: If by reprimand I am removed, even with rich fields and property I still cannot keep them.

sentences.zh: 近世士大夫務廣田宅，為不肖子酒色費，我無是也。」

translations.literal: Scholars and officials of recent times strive for vast fields and houses as expense for unworthy sons in wine and pleasure—I have none of that."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials of recent times strive for vast fields and houses as expense for unworthy sons in wine and pleasure. I have none of that."

sentences.zh: 引萬年主簿韓朝宗為御史，卒後十餘歲，朝宗以京兆尹見帝曰：「陛下待宰相，進退皆以禮，身雖沒，子孫鹹在廷。

translations.literal: He recommended Wanian chief recorder Han Chaozong as censor; more than ten years after his death Chaozong as capital metropolitan prefect saw the Emperor and said: "Your Majesty treats chancellors—advancement and dismissal all by ritual; though the body is gone, sons and grandsons all remain at court.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Wanian chief recorder Han Chaozong as censor. More than ten years after his death, Chaozong as capital metropolitan prefect saw the Emperor and said, "Your Majesty treats chancellors with ritual in advancement and dismissal. Though the body is gone, sons and grandsons all remain at court.

sentences.zh: 張嘉貞晚一息寶符，獨未官。」

translations.literal: Zhang Jiazhen at his last breath had one infant son not yet given office."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiazhen at his last breath had one infant son not yet given office."

sentences.zh: 帝惘然，召拜左司禦率府兵曹參軍，賜名曰延賞。

translations.literal: The Emperor was moved, summoned and appointed him Assistant in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Rate Command—gave him the name Yanshang [Prolonged Fortune].
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was moved, summoned him, and appointed him Assistant in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Rate Command, giving him the name Yanshang.

sentences.zh: 延賞雖蚤孤，而博涉經史，通吏治，苗晉卿尤器許，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Though Yanshang was orphaned early, he ranged widely through the classics and histories and mastered civil administration; Miao Jinqing especially prized and trusted him and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Though Yanshang was orphaned early, he ranged widely through the classics and histories and mastered civil administration. Miao Jinqing especially prized and trusted him and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 肅宗在鳳翔，擢監察御史，辟署關內節度使王思禮府。

translations.literal: When Suzong was at Fengxiang he was promoted investigating censor and joined the staff of Guannei military commissioner Wang Silì.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong was at Fengxiang he was promoted investigating censor and joined the staff of Guannei military commissioner Wang Silì.

sentences.zh: 思禮守北都，表為副，入遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: When Silì guarded the northern capital he memorialized him as deputy and he entered the capital promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Silì guarded the northern capital he memorialized him as deputy. He then entered the capital and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 始，元載被用，以晉卿力，故厚遇延賞，薦為給事中、御史中丞。

translations.literal: At first when Yuan Zai was employed, because of Jinqing's power he therefore treated Yanshang generously, recommending him as drafting attendant and chief investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yuan Zai was employed, because of Jinqing's influence he treated Yanshang generously and recommended him as drafting attendant and chief investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，除河南尹、諸道營田副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era he was made Henan metropolitan prefect and deputy commissioner of circuit field administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dali era he was made Henan metropolitan prefect and deputy commissioner of circuit field administration.

sentences.zh: 河、洛當兵沖，邑裏墟榛，延賞政簡約，輕傜賦，疏河渠，築宮廟。

translations.literal: The Yellow River and Luoyang lay on the military thoroughfare; towns and hamlets were ruined wastes; Yanshang's government was simple and restrained—light corvée levies, dredged canals, built palace temples.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River region and Luoyang lay on the military thoroughfare, and towns and hamlets were ruined wastes. Yanshang governed with simplicity and restraint, lightening corvée levies, dredging canals, and building palace temples.

sentences.zh: 數年，流庸歸附，都闕完雄，有詔褒美。

translations.literal: Within several years wandering subjects returned and attached themselves; the capital was complete and strong; there was an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Within several years wandering subjects returned and attached themselves. The capital was restored and strong, and there was an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 時罷河南、山南等副元帥，兵屯東都，詔延賞知留守，以兵屬。

translations.literal: At the time the deputy chief commanders of Henan, Shannan, and other circuits were abolished; troops were stationed at the eastern capital; an edict made Yanshang know retainership and placed the army under him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the deputy chief commanders of Henan, Shannan, and other circuits were abolished. Troops were stationed at the eastern capital, and an edict made Yanshang know retainership and placed the army under him.

sentences.zh: 居五年，治行第一，召還。

translations.literal: After five years in office his administration ranked first; he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After five years in office his administration ranked first, and he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 會李少良劾元載陰罪，載斥其狂，下御史臺治訊，而延賞適拜大夫，不滿所私，出為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: When Li Shaoliang impeached Yuan Zai's secret crimes, Zai denounced him as mad and sent him to the censorate for interrogation; just then Yanshang was appointed chief censor—displeased he was not Zai's man, he was sent out as Huainan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shaoliang impeached Yuan Zai's secret crimes, Zai denounced him as mad and sent him to the censorate for interrogation. Just then Yanshang was appointed chief censor. Displeased that he was not Zai's man, Zai sent him out as Huainan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，民它遷，吏禁之。

translations.literal: The year was drought-stricken and the people migrated elsewhere; officials forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: The year was drought-stricken and the people migrated elsewhere, but officials forbade it.

sentences.zh: 延賞曰：「食者，人恃以活。

translations.literal: Yanshang said: "Food is what people rely on to live.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang said, "Food is what people rely on to live.

sentences.zh: 拘此而斃，不如適彼而生。

translations.literal: To detain them here and let them die is not as good as going elsewhere to live.
translations.idiomatic: To detain them here and let them die is not as good as going elsewhere to live.

sentences.zh: 茍存吾人，何限為？」

translations.literal: So long as our people survive, what need to set limits?"
translations.idiomatic: So long as our people survive, what need to set limits?"

sentences.zh: 乃具舟遣之，敕吏為修室廬，已逋債，而歸者更增於舊。

translations.literal: He therefore provided boats to send them off, ordered officials to repair houses for them, forgive past debts—and those who returned increased beyond what had been before.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore provided boats to send them off, ordered officials to repair houses for them and forgive past debts, and those who returned increased beyond what had been before.

sentences.zh: 瓜步舟艫津湊，而遙系江南，延賞請度屬揚州，自是行無稽壅。

translations.literal: At Guabu the boats and barges jammed the ford yet were bound distantly to Jiangnan; Yanshang requested they be placed under Yangzhou's jurisdiction, and from then on transit went without hindrance.
translations.idiomatic: At Guabu boats and barges jammed the ford yet were bound distantly to Jiangnan. Yanshang requested they be placed under Yangzhou's jurisdiction, and from then on transit went without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 會母喪免，服除，累拜荊南、劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was dismissed for mourning; when mourning ended he was repeatedly appointed military commissioner of Jingnan and Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was dismissed for mourning. When mourning ended he was repeatedly appointed military commissioner of Jingnan and Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 建中中，西山兵馬使張朏襲成都為亂，延賞奔鹿頭戌。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era, Western Mountain military horse commissioner Zhang Fei attacked Chengdu in revolt, and Yanshang fled to Lutos Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianzhong era, Western Mountain military horse commissioner Zhang Fei attacked Chengdu in revolt, and Yanshang fled to Lutos Fort.

sentences.zh: 朏酣亂不設備，延賞諜知之，遣將叱幹遂捕斬朏，復成都。

translations.literal: Fei was drunk amid disorder and set no guard; Yanshang learned this through spies, sent the general Chi Gan to capture and behead Fei, and recovered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Fei was drunk amid disorder and set no guard. Yanshang learned this through spies, sent General Chi Gan to capture and behead Fei, and recovered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 自楊國忠討南蠻，三蜀疲罄。

translations.literal: From Yang Guozhong's campaign against the southern barbarians, the Three Shu were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: From Yang Guozhong's campaign against the southern barbarians, the Three Shu were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 及乘輿臨狩，糜用百出。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage went south on inspection, disbursements came out by the hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage went south on inspection, disbursements came out by the hundred.

sentences.zh: 後更郭英軿、崔寧、楊子琳亂，益矜僭，公私蕭然。

translations.literal: Later Guo Yingyi, Cui Ning, and Yang Zilin revolted in succession, growing ever arrogant and presumptuous, and public and private affairs were bleak.
translations.idiomatic: Later Guo Yingyi, Cui Ning, and Yang Zilin revolted in succession, growing ever arrogant and presumptuous, until public and private affairs were bleak.

sentences.zh: 延賞事為之制，薄入謹出，府庫遂實。

translations.literal: Yanshang set regulations for affairs—thin income and careful outgo—and the treasuries became full.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang set regulations for affairs—thin income and careful outgo—and the treasuries became full.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天，貢獻踵道。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, tribute and gifts crowded the roads.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong was at Fengtian, tribute and gifts crowded the roads.

sentences.zh: 及次梁，倚劍蜀為根本。

translations.literal: When he halted at Liang, he relied on sword-Shu as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: When he halted at Liang, he relied on sword-Shu as his foundation.

sentences.zh: 即拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate Commissioner with the same authority as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate Commissioner with the same authority as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝還，詔入秉政。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned, an edict summoned him to take charge of government.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned, an edict summoned him to take charge of government.

sentences.zh: 初，吐藩寇劍南，李晟總神策軍戌之，及還，以成都倡自隨，延賞遣吏奪取，故晟銜之；

translations.literal: At first, when Tibetans raided Jiannan, Li Sheng commanded the Divine Strategy Army to guard there; on his return he took Chengdu entertainers with him, and Yanshang sent clerks to seize them, so Sheng harbored resentment;
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Tibetans raided Jiannan, Li Sheng commanded the Divine Strategy Army to guard there. On his return he took Chengdu entertainers with him, and Yanshang sent clerks to seize them, so Sheng harbored resentment;

sentences.zh: 至是，鎮鳳翔，帝所倚重，表陳宿憾，帝不得已，罷延賞為尚書左仆射，然雅意決用之，以晟嘗為韓滉識擢，命滉移書道意。

translations.literal: By then he was stationed at Fengxiang, heavily relied on by the Emperor; he memorialized his old grievance, and the Emperor had no choice but to dismiss Yanshang as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, yet his private intention was firmly to use him; because Sheng had once been recognized and promoted by Han Huang, he ordered Huang to write conveying his intent.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sheng was stationed at Fengxiang and heavily relied on by the Emperor. He memorialized his old grievance, and the Emperor had no choice but to dismiss Yanshang as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, yet still intended firmly to use him. Because Sheng had once been recognized and promoted by Han Huang, the Emperor ordered Huang to write conveying his intent.

sentences.zh: 及俱入朝，滉從容邀晟平憾，且使薦延賞於帝，於是復拜平章事。

translations.literal: When both entered court, Huang calmly invited Sheng to smooth their resentment and had him recommend Yanshang to the Emperor; thereby he was again appointed Associate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When both entered court, Huang calmly invited Sheng to smooth their resentment and had him recommend Yanshang to the Emperor, and Yanshang was again appointed Associate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既而宴禁中，帝出瑞錦一端分系之，以示和解。

translations.literal: Soon after, at a banquet in the forbidden precinct, the Emperor brought out one length of auspicious brocade and divided it among them to show reconciliation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, at a banquet in the forbidden precinct, the Emperor brought out one length of auspicious brocade and divided it among them to show reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 晟因為子請婚，延賞不許。

translations.literal: Sheng therefore asked marriage for his son; Yanshang would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng therefore asked marriage for his son, but Yanshang would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「吾武夫雖有舊惡，杯酒間可解。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "We military men, though we have old enmity, can resolve it over a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "We military men, though we have old enmity, can resolve it over a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 儒者難犯，外睦而內含怒，今不許婚未忘也。」

translations.literal: Scholars are hard to offend—they appear outwardly friendly yet harbor anger within; now refusing marriage shows he has not forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars are hard to offend—they appear outwardly friendly yet harbor anger within. Now refusing marriage shows he has not forgotten."

sentences.zh: 先時，吐藩尚結贊請和，晟奏戎狄無信，不可許。

translations.literal: Previously, when Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan requested peace, Sheng memorialized that the Rong and Di were not to be trusted and it could not be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, when Tibetan minister Shang Jiezan requested peace, Sheng memorialized that the Rong and Di were not to be trusted and peace could not be granted.

sentences.zh: 滉亦請調軍食峙邊，無聽和。

translations.literal: Huang also requested deploying army grain to stock the border and not listening to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Huang also requested deploying army grain to stock the border and not listening to peace.

sentences.zh: 帝疑將帥邀功生事，議未決。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected the generals were inviting merit and creating incidents, and discussion was undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspected the generals were inviting merit and creating incidents, and discussion was undecided.

sentences.zh: 會滉卒，延賞揣帝意，遂罷晟兵，奏以給事中鄭雲逵代之。

translations.literal: When Huang died, Yanshang gauged the Emperor's intent and then dismissed Sheng's army, memorializing that drafting attendant Zheng Yunkui replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang died, Yanshang gauged the Emperor's intent and then dismissed Sheng's army, memorializing that drafting attendant Zheng Yunkui replace him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「晟有社稷功，俾自擇代者。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Sheng has altars-and-states merit—let him himself choose his replacement."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Sheng has altars-and-states merit—let him choose his own replacement."

sentences.zh: 乃用邢君牙，而拜晟太尉兼中書令，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Then Xing Junya was used, while Sheng was appointed Grand Preceptor concurrent Director of the Palace Secretariat with attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xing Junya was used, while Sheng was appointed Grand Preceptor concurrent Director of the Palace Secretariat with attendance at court.

sentences.zh: 是夏，吐蕃背約，劫渾瑊，將校多沒，如晟等策。

translations.literal: That summer Tibet broke the treaty and raided Hun Jian; many officers and commanders perished—as Sheng and others had strategized.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Tibet broke the treaty and raided Hun Jian; many officers and commanders perished, as Sheng and others had strategized.

sentences.zh: 故事，臨軒冊拜三公，中書令讀冊，侍中贊禮，或闕，則宰相攝事。

translations.literal: By precedent, when enfeoffing the Three Dukes at the Hall, the Director read the patent and the Minister of Rites intoned the ritual—or if one was lacking, the chancellor deputized.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when enfeoffing the Three Dukes at the Hall, the Director read the patent and the Minister of Rites intoned the ritual—or if one was lacking, the chancellor deputized.

sentences.zh: 晟當拜，而延賞薄其禮，用尚書崔漢衡、劉滋代攝。

translations.literal: When Sheng was to bow, Yanshang slighted his ritual and used Ministers of Rites Cui Hanheng and Liu Zi to deputize instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng was to bow, Yanshang slighted his ritual and used Ministers of Rites Cui Hanheng and Liu Zi to deputize instead.

sentences.zh: 時議遣劉玄佐復河、湟，延賞因建言：「今官繁費廣，州縣殘困，宜並省其員，悉收稟料糧課輸京師，賞戰士。」

translations.literal: At the time discussion was to send Liu Xuanzuo to recover He and Huang; Yanshang therefore submitted: "Now offices are numerous and expenses vast, and prefectures and counties are ravaged and distressed. Offices ought to be merged and reduced, stipends, grain, and tax levies fully collected and sent to the capital, and fighting warriors rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: At the time discussion was to send Liu Xuanzuo to recover He and Huang. Yanshang therefore submitted, "Now offices are numerous and expenses vast, and prefectures and counties are ravaged and distressed. Offices ought to be merged and reduced, stipends, grain, and tax levies fully collected and sent to the capital, and fighting warriors rewarded."

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 即詔：「上州留上佐、錄事參軍、司戶、司兵、司士各一員，余參軍留半；

translations.literal: An edict at once said: "In superior prefectures retain one each of senior assistant, recording secretary, revenue registrar, military registrar, and clerical registrar; other assistants retain half;
translations.idiomatic: An edict at once said, "In superior prefectures retain one each of senior assistant, recording secretary, revenue registrar, military registrar, and clerical registrar; other assistants retain half;

sentences.zh: 中州減司士；

translations.literal: in middle prefectures reduce the clerical registrar;
translations.idiomatic: in middle prefectures reduce the clerical registrar;

sentences.zh: 上縣令、尉具；

translations.literal: in superior counties retain magistrate and defender;
translations.idiomatic: in superior counties retain magistrate and defender;

sentences.zh: 中縣省尉；

translations.literal: in middle counties eliminate the defender;
translations.idiomatic: in middle counties eliminate the defender;

sentences.zh: 京兆、河南府司錄、判官，赤縣丞、簿、尉，各省半；

translations.literal: in Jingzhao and Henan prefectures, chief recorders and judicial officers, and in imperial counties assistants, clerks, and defenders, reduce each by half;
translations.idiomatic: in Jingzhao and Henan prefectures, chief recorders and judicial officers, and in imperial counties assistants, clerks, and defenders, reduce each by half;

sentences.zh: 余府準上州。」

translations.literal: other prefectures follow the superior prefecture standard."
translations.idiomatic: other prefectures follow the superior prefecture standard."

sentences.zh: 詔下，內外始怨。

translations.literal: When the edict descended, resentment began within and without.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict descended, resentment began within and without.

sentences.zh: 玄佐辭西討，延賞更用李抱真。

translations.literal: Xuanzuo declined the western campaign, and Yanshang again used Li Baozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzuo declined the western campaign, and Yanshang again used Li Baozhen.

sentences.zh: 抱真怨延賞奪晟兵，不肯行。

translations.literal: Baozhen resented Yanshang for seizing Sheng's army and refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen resented Yanshang for seizing Sheng's army and refused to go.

sentences.zh: 由是功臣解體。

translations.literal: Thereby meritorious ministers fell apart.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby meritorious ministers fell apart.

sentences.zh: 是年，除吏千五百員，當省者千餘。

translations.literal: That year, 1,500 office posts were eliminated, of which over a thousand should have been kept.
translations.idiomatic: That year, 1,500 office posts were eliminated, of which over a thousand should have been kept.

sentences.zh: 道路訾謗，浸淫聞於上。

translations.literal: The roads were full of slander, gradually reaching the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were full of slander, gradually reaching the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 延賞懼，請詔州縣：「或考先滿、或攝掌遇停限而官見乏者，聽在所擇省員有幹譽者權補，以才不以資。」

translations.literal: Yanshang feared this and requested an edict to prefectures and counties: "Where examination terms are already full, or acting appointments meet stop-limits while offices are visibly short, let the locality choose from reduced posts men of ability and reputation to fill provisionally, by talent not by seniority."
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang feared this and requested an edict to prefectures and counties: "Where examination terms are already full, or acting appointments meet stop-limits while offices are visibly short, let the locality choose from reduced posts men of ability and reputation to fill provisionally, by talent not by seniority."

sentences.zh: 而大臣馬燧、白誌貞、韋倫表言省官太甚，不可行。

translations.literal: But great ministers Ma Sui, Bai Zhiben, and Wei Lun memorialized that provincial officials were too few and it could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But great ministers Ma Sui, Bai Zhiben, and Wei Lun memorialized that provincial officials were too few and it could not be carried out.

sentences.zh: 會延賞疾困，不能事，宰相李泌一切奏復。

translations.literal: When Yanshang was gravely ill and could not conduct affairs, Chancellor Li Mi memorialized restoring everything.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanshang was gravely ill and could not conduct affairs, Chancellor Li Mi memorialized restoring everything.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一，贈太保，謚曰成肅。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-one; posthumously made Grand Preceptor, posthumous title Chengzhu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one. He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Chengzhu.

sentences.zh: 延賞更四鎮，所至民頌其愛。

translations.literal: Yanshang changed four military commissions; wherever he went the people praised his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshang served four military commissions; wherever he went the people praised his kindness.

sentences.zh: 及當國，飾情復怨，不稱所望，亦早不幸，未及有所建明。

translations.literal: When he held national office he adorned his feelings and nursed old resentments, not matching what was hoped, and also died early without having been able to establish anything notable.
translations.idiomatic: When he held national office he adorned his feelings and nursed old resentments, not matching what was hoped, and also died early without having been able to establish anything notable.

sentences.zh: 然帝待遇厚，稱其奏議有宰相體，專屬以吏事，而以軍食委李泌，刑法委柳渾，時以為任職。

translations.literal: Yet the Emperor treated him generously, saying his memorials had the manner of a chancellor; he was entrusted especially with civil administration, while military provisions were left to Li Mi and penal law to Liu Hun—at the time considered a proper division of duties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Emperor treated him generously, saying his memorials had the manner of a chancellor. He was entrusted especially with civil administration, while military provisions were left to Li Mi and penal law to Liu Hun—at the time considered a proper division of duties.

sentences.zh: 子弘靖。

translations.literal: His son was Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 弘靖字元理，雅厚信直，以蔭為河南參軍。

translations.literal: Hongjing, style name Yuanli, was refined, generous, faithful, and upright; by privilege he was made Henan assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing, style name Yuanli, was refined, generous, faithful, and upright; by privilege he was made Henan assistant.

sentences.zh: 杜亞辟佐其府。

translations.literal: Du Ya recruited him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya recruited him to his staff.

sentences.zh: 亞疑牙將令狐運劫餉絹，弘靖直其枉，亞怒，斥出府。

translations.literal: Ya suspected military tooth-commander Linghu Yun of robbing tribute silk; Hongjing upheld his innocence; Ya was angry and expelled him from the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Ya suspected military tooth-commander Linghu Yun of robbing tribute silk. Hongjing upheld his innocence, and Ya was angry and expelled him from the staff.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡為德陽公主治第，欲徙弘靖先廟，上疏自言，德宗異之，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling was building a residence for Princess Deyang and wished to move Hongjing's ancestral temple; Hongjing submitted a memorial on his own behalf; Dezong was struck by it and promoted him investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling was building a residence for Princess Deyang and wished to move Hongjing's ancestral temple. Hongjing submitted a memorial on his own behalf, and Dezong was struck by it and promoted him investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部侍郎、陜州觀察使，徙河中節度使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Shaanzhou observation commissioner, then transferred to Hedong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Shaanzhou observation commissioner, then transferred to Hedong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元和中，拜刑部尚書同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he was appointed Minister of Punishments and Associate Commissioner with the same authority as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanhe era he was appointed Minister of Punishments and Associate Commissioner with the same authority as chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 吳少陽死，其子元濟擅總留務，憲宗欲誅之。

translations.literal: Wu Shaoyang died; his son Yuanji seized control of the acting commission; Xianzong wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoyang died, and his son Yuanji seized control of the acting commission. Xianzong wished to execute him.

sentences.zh: 弘靖請先遣使者吊贈，待不恭，乃加兵，詔可。

translations.literal: Hongjing requested first sending envoys to offer condolences and gifts; if Yuanji were disrespectful, then add troops; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing requested first sending envoys to offer condolences and gifts; if Yuanji were disrespectful, then add troops. The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 進中書侍郎，封高平縣侯。

translations.literal: He was promoted Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and enfeoffed Marquis of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and enfeoffed Marquis of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 武元衡遇害，賊未得，王承宗邸廝卒張晏被告，詔付御史臺劾驗，有狀。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanheng was murdered the culprit was not yet found; Wang Chengzong's lodge servant Zhang Yan was accused; an edict sent him to the censorate for investigation, and there was evidence.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanheng was murdered the culprit was not yet found. Wang Chengzong's lodge servant Zhang Yan was accused, and an edict sent him to the censorate for investigation, where evidence was found.

sentences.zh: 弘靖疑御史傅致晏罪，言之帝，不聽，遂誅晏，並討承宗。

translations.literal: Hongjing suspected the censor had fabricated Yan's guilt and spoke to the Emperor; the Emperor would not listen, and Yan was executed while Chengzong was also attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing suspected the censor had fabricated Yan's guilt and spoke to the Emperor. The Emperor would not listen, and Yan was executed while Chengzong was also attacked.

sentences.zh: 弘靖曰：「戎事並興，鮮有濟。

translations.literal: Hongjing said, "When military affairs rise together, success is rare.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing said, "When military affairs rise together, success is rare.

sentences.zh: 不如悉力淮西，已平，乃治河朔。」

translations.literal: It is better to concentrate all strength on Huai West; once that is pacified, then deal with Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: It is better to concentrate all strength on Huai West. Once that is pacified, then deal with Hebei."

sentences.zh: 議再迕，乃歸政，以檢校吏部尚書、同平章事，為河東節度使。

translations.literal: Discussion clashed again, and he returned power, made Acting Minister of Personnel and Associate Commissioner, and became Hedong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion clashed again, and he returned power, was made Acting Minister of Personnel and Associate Commissioner, and became Hedong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未及鎮，詔伐承宗。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, an edict ordered an attack on Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, an edict ordered an attack on Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 弘靖自以諫不聽，思自效，乃大閱兵，請身討賊。

translations.literal: Hongjing, thinking his advice had not been heeded, wished to prove himself and therefore reviewed troops on a great scale, requesting to go in person to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing, thinking his advice had not been heeded, wished to prove himself and therefore reviewed troops on a great scale, requesting to go in person to attack the rebels.

sentences.zh: 詔許出軍，無親往。

translations.literal: An edict permitted sending out the army but not going in person.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted sending out the army but not going in person.

sentences.zh: 既王師無功，帝憶曩言，下詔褒美。

translations.literal: When the imperial army achieved nothing, the Emperor recalled his earlier words and issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army achieved nothing, the Emperor recalled his earlier words and issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 弘靖亦遣使間道喻承宗，承宗款附。

translations.literal: Hongjing also sent an envoy by a secret route to persuade Chengzong, and Chengzong submitted in sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing also sent an envoy by a secret route to persuade Chengzong, and Chengzong submitted in sincerity.

sentences.zh: 召拜吏部尚書，徙節宣武。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, then transferred to the Xuanwu commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, then transferred to the Xuanwu commission.

sentences.zh: 宣武承韓弘虐政，代以寬簡，民便安之。

translations.literal: Xuanwu had inherited Han Hong's harsh government; Hongjing replaced it with leniency and simplicity, and the people were eased and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu had inherited Han Hong's harsh government. Hongjing replaced it with leniency and simplicity, and the people were eased and settled.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，劉總舉所部內屬，請弘靖為代，進檢校司空，仍同中書門下平章事，充盧龍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing era Liu Zong offered his command inward and requested Hongjing as replacement; he was promoted Acting Minister of Works, still Associate Commissioner, and made Lulong military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Changqing era Liu Zong offered his command inward and requested Hongjing as replacement. He was promoted Acting Minister of Works, still Associate Commissioner, and made Lulong military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 始入幽州，老幼夾道觀。

translations.literal: When he first entered Youzhou, old and young lined the roads to watch.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered Youzhou, old and young lined the roads to watch.

sentences.zh: 河朔舊將與士卒均寒暑，無障蓋安輿，弘靖素貴，肩輿而行，人駭異。

translations.literal: Hebei's old generals shared heat and cold with the soldiers and had no screened carriage or comfortable litter; Hongjing had always been noble and traveled in a shoulder litter, and people were startled.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei's old generals shared heat and cold with the soldiers and had no screened carriage or comfortable litter. Hongjing had always been noble and traveled in a shoulder litter, and people were startled.

sentences.zh: 俗謂祿山、思明為「二聖」，弘靖懲始亂，欲變其俗，乃發墓毀棺，眾滋不悅。

translations.literal: The custom called An Lushan and Shi Siming the "Two Sages"; Hongjing, punishing the origin of disorder, wished to change the custom and therefore opened their tombs and destroyed their coffins, and the multitude grew more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The custom called An Lushan and Shi Siming the "Two Sages." Hongjing, punishing the origin of disorder, wished to change the custom and therefore opened their tombs and destroyed their coffins, and the multitude grew more displeased.

sentences.zh: 旬一決事，賓客將吏罕聞其言。

translations.literal: Once every ten days he decided affairs; guests, staff, and officers rarely heard him speak.
translations.idiomatic: Once every ten days he decided affairs; guests, staff, and officers rarely heard him speak.

sentences.zh: 委成於參佐韋雍、張宗厚，又不通大體，朘刻軍賜，專以法拫治之。

translations.literal: He entrusted power to aides Wei Yong and Zhang Zonghou, who also did not grasp the larger pattern, pared military rewards, and governed solely by harsh law.
translations.idiomatic: He entrusted power to aides Wei Yong and Zhang Zonghou, who also did not grasp the larger pattern, pared military rewards, and governed solely by harsh law.

sentences.zh: 官屬輕侻酣肆，夜歸，燭火滿街，前後呵止，其詬責士皆曰「反虜」，嘗曰：「天下無事，而輩挽兩石弓，不如識一丁字。」

translations.literal: Subordinates were frivolous and drunken; returning at night, candles filled the streets, and when halted before and behind they reviled the soldiers as "rebel bandits," saying, "When all is calm under Heaven, yet you draw two-stone bows, you might as well know one character."
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates were frivolous and drunken. Returning at night, candles filled the streets, and when halted before and behind they reviled the soldiers as "rebel bandits," saying, "When all is calm under Heaven, yet you draw two-stone bows, you might as well know one character."

sentences.zh: 軍中以氣自任，銜之。

translations.literal: The army, proud by temperament, harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The army, proud by temperament, harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 總之朝，詔以錢百萬緡賚將士，弘靖取二十萬市府雜費，有怨言。

translations.literal: When Zong came to court, an edict granted a million strings of cash to reward the soldiers; Hongjing took two hundred thousand for prefectural miscellaneous expenses, and there were complaints.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong came to court, an edict granted a million strings of cash to reward the soldiers. Hongjing took two hundred thousand for prefectural miscellaneous expenses, and there were complaints.

sentences.zh: 會雍欲鞭小將，薊人未嘗更笞辱，不伏，弘靖系之。

translations.literal: When Yong wished to flog a young officer, the people of Ji had never before suffered beating and insult, and would not submit; Hongjing had him bound.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong wished to flog a young officer, the people of Ji had never before suffered beating and insult and would not submit. Hongjing had him bound.

sentences.zh: 是夕軍亂，囚弘靖薊門館，掠其家貲婢妾，執雍等殺之。

translations.literal: That night the army mutinied, imprisoned Hongjing at the Ji Gate lodge, plundered his family wealth, concubines, and maidservants, and seized Yong and others and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: That night the army mutinied, imprisoned Hongjing at the Ji Gate lodge, plundered his family wealth, concubines, and maidservants, and seized Yong and others and killed them.

sentences.zh: 判官張澈始就職，得不殺，與弘靖同被囚。

translations.literal: Judicial officer Zhang Che had just taken office and was not killed; he was imprisoned together with Hongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial officer Zhang Che had just taken office and was not killed; he was imprisoned together with Hongjing.

sentences.zh: 會詔使至，澈謂弘靖曰：「公無負此土人，今天子使至，可因見眾辨，幸得脫歸。」

translations.literal: When the edict envoy arrived, Che said to Hongjing, "You have not failed the people of this land. Today the Son of Heaven's envoy has come—you can use the occasion to face the multitude and explain yourself and perhaps escape and return."
translations.idiomatic: When the edict envoy arrived, Che said to Hongjing, "You have not failed the people of this land. Today the Son of Heaven's envoy has come—you can use the occasion to face the multitude and explain yourself and perhaps escape and return."

sentences.zh: 即推門求出。

translations.literal: He at once pushed open the door and sought to go out.
translations.idiomatic: He at once pushed open the door and sought to go out.

sentences.zh: 眾畏其謀，欲遷別館。

translations.literal: The multitude feared his plot and wished to move them to another lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude feared his plot and wished to move them to another lodge.

sentences.zh: 澈大罵曰：「汝何敢反！

translations.literal: Che cursed loudly, "How dare you rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Che cursed loudly, "How dare you rebel!

sentences.zh: 前日吳元濟斬東市，李師道斬軍中，同惡者，父母妻子肉飽狗鼠鴟鴉。」

translations.literal: Earlier Wu Yuanji was beheaded at the eastern market and Li Shidao in the army camp—men of the same evil; their fathers, mothers, wives, and children became meat to glut dogs, rats, kites, and crows."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wu Yuanji was beheaded at the eastern market and Li Shidao in the army camp—men of the same evil. Their fathers, mothers, wives, and children became meat to glut dogs, rats, kites, and crows."

sentences.zh: 眾怒，擊殺之。

translations.literal: The multitude was enraged and struck him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude was enraged and struck him to death.

sentences.zh: 數日，吏卒稍自悔，詣館謝弘靖，願革心事之。

translations.literal: After several days officers and soldiers gradually repented themselves and came to the lodge to apologize to Hongjing, wishing to reform their hearts and serve him.
translations.idiomatic: After several days officers and soldiers gradually repented themselves and came to the lodge to apologize to Hongjing, wishing to reform their hearts and serve him.

sentences.zh: 三請，不對。

translations.literal: Three times they asked; he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Three times they asked; he did not answer.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「公不赦我矣，軍中可一日無帥乎？」

translations.literal: The multitude said, "You will not pardon us—can the army be without a commander for even one day?"
translations.idiomatic: The multitude said, "You will not pardon us—can the army be without a commander for even one day?"

sentences.zh: 遂取朱克融主留後。

translations.literal: They therefore took Zhu Kerong to head the acting commission.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore took Zhu Kerong to head the acting commission.

sentences.zh: 詔貶弘靖太子賓客。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Hongjing to Crown Prince's Guest.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Hongjing to Crown Prince's Guest.

sentences.zh: 分司東都。

translations.literal: He served in the eastern-capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the eastern-capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 再貶吉州刺史。

translations.literal: He was demoted again to prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，出幽州，改撫州刺史，稍遷太子少師。

translations.literal: The next year he left Youzhou, was changed to prefect of Fuzhou, and was gradually promoted Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he left Youzhou, was changed to prefect of Fuzhou, and was gradually promoted Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十五，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-five; posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-five and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 弘靖少有令問，杜鴻漸、杜佑皆器許。

translations.literal: Hongjing in youth had a fine reputation; Du Hongjian and Du You both prized and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjing in youth had a fine reputation; Du Hongjian and Du You both prized and trusted him.

sentences.zh: 歷臺閣顯級，人以為有輔相才。

translations.literal: He held prominent posts at court and terrace, and people thought he had assistant-minister talent.
translations.idiomatic: He held prominent posts at court and terrace, and people thought he had assistant-minister talent.

sentences.zh: 及居位，簡默自處，無所規拂。

translations.literal: Once in office he was quiet and self-contained, without corrections or rejections.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office he was quiet and self-contained, without corrections or rejections.

sentences.zh: 幽薊初效順，不能因俗制變，故范陽復亂。

translations.literal: You and Ji at first submitted in obedience, but he could not adapt institutions according to local custom; therefore Fanyang rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: When You and Ji first submitted, he failed to adapt governance to local ways, and Fanyang rose in rebellion once more.

sentences.zh: 家聚書畫，侔秘府。

translations.literal: The household amassed books and paintings, rivaling the secret archive.
translations.idiomatic: The family collected books and paintings to rival the imperial archive.

sentences.zh: 先第在東都思順裏，盛麗甲當時，歷五世無所增葺，時號「三相張家」雲。

translations.literal: The ancestral mansion stood in Sishun Lane of the Eastern Capital, splendid beyond any of the age; through five generations none added or repaired it, and contemporaries called it the "Three-Chancellors Zhang Family," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Their ancestral estate in Sishun Lane of the Eastern Capital was the grandest of the day; for five generations no one enlarged or renovated it, and men of the time spoke of the "Three-Chancellors Zhang Family."

sentences.zh: 子：文規、次宗。

translations.literal: Sons: Wengui and Cizong.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Wengui and Cizong.

sentences.zh: 裴度秉政，引文規為右補闕。

translations.literal: When Pei Du held power, he brought in Wengui as Right Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: While Pei Du directed the government, he appointed Wengui Right Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 度出襄陽，貶溫令，度奏置幕府。

translations.literal: When Du went out to Xiangyang, [Wengui] was demoted to magistrate of Wen; Du memorialized to place him on the secretariat staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Du was posted to Xiangyang, Wengui was demoted to magistrate of Wen, and Du had him assigned to his staff.

sentences.zh: 累轉吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: Through successive transfers he became Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 右丞韋溫劾文規父昔被囚，逗留不赴難，不宜任省署。

translations.literal: Vice Director Wei Wen impeached Wengui, [saying] his father in the past had been imprisoned and [Wengui] lingered without going to the crisis; he was unfit to serve in the central office.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wei Wen impeached Wengui on the ground that his father had once been imprisoned and Wengui had lingered away rather than answer the crisis, making him unfit for a post in the central administration.

sentences.zh: 出為安州刺史，終桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as prefect of Anzhou and ended as Military Governor of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as prefect of Anzhou and ended his career as military governor of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 子彥遠，博學有文辭，乾符中至大理卿。

translations.literal: His son Yanyuan was broadly learned and had literary skill; in the Qianfu era he rose to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanyuan was erudite and accomplished in letters; during the Qianfu era he reached the post of Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 次宗，開成初為起居舍人。

translations.literal: Cizong, at the start of Kaicheng, served as Recorder of the Emperor's Movements and Residences.
translations.idiomatic: Cizong served as Recorder of the Emperor's Movements and Residences at the beginning of the Kaicheng era.

sentences.zh: 文宗始詔左右史立螭頭下記宰相奏對，既退，帝召見審正是非。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong first ordered the Left and Right Historians to stand below the chih-head and record the chancellors' presentations and responses; after they withdrew, the Emperor summoned them to verify right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong first commanded the Left and Right Historians to stand beneath the chih-head and record the chancellors' exchanges with the throne; when they withdrew, he summoned them back to confirm whether the record was correct.

sentences.zh: 故開成時事為最詳。

translations.literal: Therefore affairs of the Kaicheng era are recorded most fully.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the events of the Kaicheng era are recorded in the greatest detail.

sentences.zh: 以稱職，兼集賢院直學士。

translations.literal: Because of competent service, he was additionally made Direct Scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Recognized for competent service, he was also appointed Direct Scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 文規左遷，改國子博士、史館修撰。

translations.literal: When Wengui was demoted and transferred, [Cizong was] changed to National University Erudite and Compiler at the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Wengui was demoted and transferred, Cizong was reassigned as National University Erudite and compiler at the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 李德裕再當國，引為考功員外郎，知制誥。

translations.literal: When Li Deyu again held the reins of state, he brought [Cizong] in as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel's Evaluations Bureau, with charge of drafting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Deyu again directed the government, he brought Cizong in as Vice Director of the Evaluations Bureau in the Ministry of Personnel, with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 出澧、明二州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Li and Ming [prefectures] and died.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Li and Ming and died in office.

sentences.zh: 孫茂樞，字休府，及進士第。

translations.literal: His grandson Maoshu, courtesy name Xiufu, attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Maoshu, styled Xiufu, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，累遷祠部郎中，知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Tianyou era, through successive promotions he became Director in the Ministry of Rites' Sacrifices Bureau, with charge of drafting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianyou era he rose through successive promotions to Director in the Sacrifices Bureau of the Ministry of Rites, with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 坐柳璨事，貶博昌尉。

translations.literal: Because of the Liu Can affair, he was demoted to magistrate of Bochang.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in the Liu Can affair, he was demoted to magistrate of Bochang.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐，嘉貞弟，有幹略。

translations.literal: Jiayou, younger brother of Jiazhen, had capacity and strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou, Jiazhen's younger brother, possessed ability and strategic talent.

sentences.zh: 方嘉貞為相時，任右金吾衛將軍，昆弟每上朝，軒蓋騶導盈閭巷。

translations.literal: When Jiazhen was chancellor, [Jiayou] served as General of the Right Gold Crow Guard; whenever the brothers went to court, carriage canopies and outrunner escorts filled the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: While Jiazhen was chancellor, Jiayou held the post of General of the Right Gold Crow Guard; each time the brothers attended court, their carriages and outrunners filled the lanes.

sentences.zh: 時號所居坊曰「鳴珂裏」。

translations.literal: The age called the ward where they lived "Mingke Lane."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time called the ward where they lived "Mingke Lane."

sentences.zh: 後貶浦陽府折沖。

translations.literal: Later he was demoted to Area Commander of Puyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later demoted to area commander of Puyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開元末，為相州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, he was prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Kaiyuan era he served as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊刺史多死官，眾疑畏。

translations.literal: Former prefects mostly died in office; the people were suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Previous prefects had mostly died in office, and the people were filled with dread and suspicion.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐以周總管尉遲迥死國難，忠臣也，立祠房解祓眾心。

translations.literal: Jiayou held that Zhou's Chief Administrator Yuchi Jiong had died in the state's crisis—a loyal minister—and built a shrine chamber to cleanse and dispel the people's fears.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou argued that Yuchi Jiong, chief administrator under Northern Zhou, had died in the state's service and was a loyal minister; he built a shrine chamber to perform rites of purification and lay the people's fears to rest.

sentences.zh: 三歲，入為左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: After three years, he entered [the capital] as General of the Left Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he entered the capital as General of the Left Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 後吳克為刺史，又加神冕服，遂無患。

translations.literal: Later when Wu Ke became prefect, [he] also added divine crown and robes [to the shrine], and thereafter there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Wu Ke became prefect, he also added divine crown and robes to the shrine, and from then on there was no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 源乾曜，相州臨漳人。

translations.literal: Yuan Qianyao was a native of Linzhang in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Qianyao came from Linzhang in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖師民，隋刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shimin was Vice Minister of Justice under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shimin had served the Sui as Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 父直心，高宗時太常伯，流死嶺南。

translations.literal: His father Zhixin, under Emperor Gaozong was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; he was exiled and died in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixin had been Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under Emperor Gaozong; he was exiled and died in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 乾曜第進士。

translations.literal: Qianyao passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao obtained the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，以殿中侍御史黜陟江東，奏課最，頻遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era, as Palace Censor he assessed promotion and demotion in Jiangdong; his memorial on evaluation ranked highest, and he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he served as Palace Censor assessing promotions and demotions in Jiangdong; his report on official performance ranked highest, and he was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 景雲後，公卿百官上巳、九日廢射禮，乾曜以為：「聖王教天下必制禮以正人情。

translations.literal: After Jingyun, the high ministers and hundred officials abolished archery rites on the Third Day of the Third Month and the Double Ninth; Qianyao held that: "The sage kings in teaching the empire must establish rites to set right human sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jingyun era, ministers and officials ceased the archery rites held on the Third Day of the Third Month and the Double Ninth; Qianyao argued: "When sage kings instruct the empire, they must establish rites to correct human conduct.

sentences.zh: 君子三年不為禮，禮必壞；

translations.literal: If the gentleman for three years makes no rite, rites must decay;
translations.idiomatic: If for three years no rites are performed, the rites themselves decay;

sentences.zh: 三年不為樂，樂必崩。

translations.literal: for three years he makes no music, music must collapse.
translations.idiomatic: and if for three years no music is made, music collapses.

sentences.zh: 古之擇士，先觀射禮，非取一時樂也。

translations.literal: In antiquity in selecting officers, one first observed the archery rite—not taking momentary pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when choosing officers, one first observed the archery rite; it was not undertaken for momentary amusement.

sentences.zh: 夫射者，別邪正，觀德行，中祭祀，辟寇戎，古先哲王莫不遞襲。

translations.literal: Now archery distinguishes the crooked from the straight, reveals conduct and virtue, serves in sacrifices, and repels invaders and enemies—none of the sage kings of old failed to transmit it in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Archery separates the crooked from the straight, reveals character and virtue, supports sacrifice, and repels invaders—no sage king of old ever failed to pass it down in turn.

sentences.zh: 比年以來，射禮不講，所司丱費，而舊典為虧。

translations.literal: In recent years the archery rite is not practiced; the responsible offices act perfunctorily and waste resources, while the old canon is diminished.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the archery rite has fallen into neglect; the offices responsible have grown careless and wasteful, and the ancient institutions have been eroded.

sentences.zh: 臣愚謂所計者財，所虧者禮，故孔子不愛羊而存禮也。

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly considers: what is counted is wealth, what is diminished is rite; therefore Confucius did not spare the sheep but preserved the rite.
translations.idiomatic: I would humbly suggest that what is being weighed is money, but what is being lost is ritual propriety—just as Confucius chose to keep the rite rather than save the sacrificial sheep.

sentences.zh: 大射謂春秋不可廢。」
