translations.literal: Great archery—I say the spring and autumn [rites] must not be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: As for the great archery rite, I submit that it must not be abandoned in spring and autumn."

sentences.zh: 開元初，邠王府吏犯法，玄宗敕左右為王求才長史，太常卿姜交薦乾曜，自梁州都督召見，神氣爽澈，占對有序，帝悅之，擢少府少監，兼邠王府長史。

translations.literal: In early Kaiyuan, an official of the Prince of Bin's household violated the law; Emperor Xuanzong ordered his attendants to find a talented chief secretary for the prince; Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao recommended Qianyao; summoned from his post as Area Commander of Liangzhou and received in audience, his spirit was bright and clear and his replies were orderly; the Emperor was pleased, promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and concurrently made him Chief Secretary of the Prince of Bin's household.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaiyuan, when an official of the Prince of Bin's household broke the law, Emperor Xuanzong ordered his attendants to find a capable chief secretary for the prince. Jiang Jiao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, recommended Qianyao; summoned from his post as area commander of Liangzhou and received in audience, Qianyao appeared keen and lucid and answered in good order. The Emperor was pleased, promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, and concurrently appointed him chief secretary of the Prince of Bin's household.

sentences.zh: 累進尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，拜黃門侍郎、同紫微黃門平章事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Privy Councilor of the Palace Administration and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and concurrent Privy Councilor of the Palace Administration and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 逾月，與姚崇俱罷。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he and Yao Chong were both dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a month later, he and Yao Chong were both removed from office.

sentences.zh: 會帝東幸，以京兆尹留守京師。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went east on tour, as Capital Magistrate he remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor toured east, Qianyao remained behind as Capital Magistrate to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 治尚寬簡，人安之。

translations.literal: His governance favored leniency and simplicity; the people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and simplicity, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 居三年，政如始至。

translations.literal: For three years his administration was as when he first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office, his administration was unchanged from the day he arrived.

sentences.zh: 仗內白鷹因縱失之，詔京兆督捕，獲於野，絓榛死。

translations.literal: An imperial white hawk from within the guard formation was lost when released for flight; an edict ordered the Capital Magistrate to supervise its capture; it was taken in the wild, entangled in hazel and dead.
translations.idiomatic: A white hawk kept within the imperial guard was lost when released to fly; the Emperor ordered the Capital Magistrate to oversee its capture. The bird was found in the wild, caught in hazel brush, and dead.

sentences.zh: 吏懼得罪，乾曜曰：「上仁明，不以畜玩置罪，茍其獲戾，尹專之。」

translations.literal: The clerks feared punishment; Qianyao said: "The Emperor is benevolent and clear-sighted; he does not punish over domestic playthings. If blame must be taken, the Magistrate alone shall bear it."
translations.idiomatic: The clerks feared they would be punished; Qianyao said, "The Emperor is benevolent and discerning and will not condemn men over a pet bird. If anyone must be blamed, let the Magistrate bear it alone."

sentences.zh: 遂入自劾失旨。

translations.literal: He then entered and submitted a self-impeachment for failing the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: He then went in and submitted a self-impeachment for having failed the Emperor's command.

sentences.zh: 帝一不問，眾伏其知體而善引咎。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not inquire once; all admired his grasp of propriety and his skill at accepting blame.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor never questioned him at all, and everyone admired his sense of propriety and his willingness to accept blame.

sentences.zh: 八年，復為黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品，進位侍中。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he again became Vice Director of the Chancellery and Concurrent Third Rank of the Secretariat and Chancellery, advancing to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he again became Vice Director of the Chancellery and concurrent third-rank official of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 建言：「大臣子並求京職，俊軿率任外官，非平施之道。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Ministers' sons all seek capital appointments, while men of talent are mostly assigned to outer posts—this is not the way of evenhanded bestowal.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "The sons of great ministers all seek posts in the capital, while able men are mostly sent to serve outside—this is not the way to distribute office fairly.

sentences.zh: 臣三息俱任京師，請出二息補外，以示自近始。」

translations.literal: Your servant's three sons all hold posts in the capital; I request sending two sons out to fill outer posts, to show beginning with those nearest to me."
translations.idiomatic: All three of my sons hold office in the capital; I ask that two of them be sent out to outer posts, beginning with those closest to me."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 乃以子河南參軍弼為絳州司功，太祝潔為鄭尉。

translations.literal: Thereupon his son Bi, Army Adjutant of Henan, was made Record Officer of Jiangzhou; his son Jie, Grand Sacrificer, was made Defender of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon his son Bi, army adjutant of Henan, was appointed record officer of Jiangzhou, and his son Jie, grand sacrificer, was appointed defender of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「乾曜身率庶寮以讓，既請外其子，又復下遷。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Qianyao personally led the multitude of officials in yielding; having requested his sons for outer service, he again demoted them downward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "Qianyao has personally led the officials in yielding; having asked that his sons be sent out, he has further demoted them.

sentences.zh: 《傳》不雲乎：『範宣子讓，其下皆讓。』

translations.literal: Does not the Record say: 'When Fan Xuanzi yielded, those below him all yielded.'
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Record say, 'When Fan Xuanzi yielded, those beneath him all yielded.'

sentences.zh: 『晉國之人，於是大和』，道之或行，仁豈遠哉。

translations.literal: 'The people of Jin thereupon achieved great harmony'—when the Way may be put into practice, how can benevolence be far?
translations.idiomatic: 'And the people of Jin were thereafter greatly harmonious.' When the Way can be practiced, is benevolence really so distant?

sentences.zh: 其令文武官父子昆弟三人在京司者，分任於外。」

translations.literal: Let all civil and military officials whose fathers and sons or brothers—three persons in capital offices—assign them separately to outer posts."
translations.idiomatic: Let every civil and military official who has three members of a father-son or brother group serving in the capital assign some of them to posts outside."

sentences.zh: 繇是公卿子弟皆出補。

translations.literal: Hence sons of the high ministers all went out to fill posts.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward, the sons of high ministers were all sent out to fill provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗自較其考，與張說偕賜。

translations.literal: The Emperor once personally compared their merit ratings, and together with Zhang Yue was granted [rewards].
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once personally reviewed their merit evaluations and granted rewards to Qianyao together with Zhang Yue.

sentences.zh: 時議者言：「國執政所以同休戚，不崇異無以責功。」

translations.literal: At the time commentators said: "The state's chief ministers share weal and woe alike; without elevating distinctions there is no means to demand merit."
translations.idiomatic: Commentators at the time said, "The chief ministers of the state share fortune and misfortune alike; unless distinctions are raised, there is no way to hold them accountable for achievement."

sentences.zh: 帝乃詔中書、門下共食實戶三百，堂封自此始。

translations.literal: The Emperor then ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery jointly to receive three hundred households of tax grain—thus began the Tang feng stipends.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then decreed that the Secretariat and Chancellery together should receive three hundred households of tax grain as stipend—thus began the institution of tang feng.

sentences.zh: 東封還，為尚書左丞相，兼侍中。

translations.literal: Returning from the eastern Feng sacrifice, he was made Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the eastern Feng sacrifice, he was appointed Left Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs, concurrently serving as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，罷侍中，遷太子少師。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was removed as Palace Attendant and transferred to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was relieved as Palace Attendant and transferred to Junior Mentor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 避祖名，更授少傅，安陽郡公。

translations.literal: To avoid his grandfather's name taboo, he was reappointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, Duke of Anyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid the taboo on his grandfather's name, he was reappointed Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and ennobled Duke of Anyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 帝幸東都，以老疾不任陪扈。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went to the Eastern Capital, [Qianyao], owing to age and illness, could not undertake escort duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital, Qianyao, owing to age and illness, was unable to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州大都督。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Great Defender-General of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Great Defender-General of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾曜性謹重，其始仕已四十餘，歷官皆以清慎恪敏得名。

translations.literal: Qianyao's nature was cautious and grave; when he first took office he was already over forty; in every post he won repute for integrity, prudence, diligence, and quickness.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyao was cautious and sober by nature; he did not enter office until he was past forty, and in every post he earned a reputation for integrity, prudence, diligence, and alert competence.

sentences.zh: 為相十年，與張嘉貞、張說、李元纮、杜暹同秉政，居中未嘗廷議可否事，晚節唯唯聯署，務為寬平惇大，故鮮咎悔。

translations.literal: As chancellor for ten years, together with Zhang Jiazhen, Zhang Yue, Li Yuanhong, and Du Xian he held power; at court he never debated whether affairs should be approved or rejected, and in his later years he merely assented and countersigned in succession, striving for leniency, simplicity, and magnanimity, and therefore rarely incurred blame or regret.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chancellor for ten years alongside Zhang Jiazhen, Zhang Yue, Li Yuanhong, and Du Xian; in court he never debated whether matters should pass or fail, and in his later years he simply assented and countersigned, seeking always to be lenient, even-handed, and broad-minded, and so he rarely drew reproach.

sentences.zh: 姜交為嘉貞所排，雖得罪，訖不申救，君子譏焉。

translations.literal: Jiang Jiao was pushed out by Jiazhen; though [Jiang] was punished, [Qianyao] to the end did not intercede—men of quality reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Jiao had been driven out by Jiazhen; although Jiang fell into disgrace, Qianyao never interceded for him, and men of judgment criticized him for it.

sentences.zh: 族孫光裕，亦有名，居官號清願，撫諸弟友義。

translations.literal: Clansman by descent Guangyu also had renown; in office he was called pure and modest; he nurtured his younger brothers with friendly righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: His clansman Guangyu was also well known; in office he was praised for purity and modesty, and he treated his younger brothers with friendly devotion.

sentences.zh: 為中書舍人，與楊滔、劉令植同刪著《開元新格》。

translations.literal: As Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat, together with Yang Tao and Liu Lingzhi he compiled and edited the New Statutes of the Kaiyuan Era.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat, he joined Yang Tao and Liu Lingzhi in compiling and editing the New Statutes of the Kaiyuan Era.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書左丞，會選諸司長官為刺史，光裕任鄭州，為世良吏。

translations.literal: He served as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; when [the court] selected directors of various bureaus to become prefects, Guangyu took Zhengzhou and was a fine official of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; when the court chose directors of various bureaus to serve as prefects, Guangyu was assigned Zhengzhou and proved a model official of the age.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while still in office.

sentences.zh: 子洧，以雍睦保家，士友推之。

translations.literal: His son Wei, through harmony and kinship preserving the household, was esteemed by scholar-friends.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei preserved the family through harmony and kinship, and was highly regarded among scholar-friends.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，為給事中、襄州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, he was Palace Recipient and prefect of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era he served as Palace Recipient and prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 安祿山犯河、洛、為江陵大都督長史以禦賊，卒，贈禮部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: When An Lushan invaded the Yellow and Luo [regions], [Wei] was made Chief Secretary to the Great Defender-General of Jiangling to repel the rebels; he died, was posthumously made Minister of Rites, posthumous name Yi (Reverent).
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan invaded the Yellow River and Luoyang regions, Wei was appointed chief secretary to the Great Defender-General of Jiangling to resist the rebels; he died in service and was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Yi (Reverent).

sentences.zh: 裴耀卿，字煥之，寧州刺史守真次子也。

translations.literal: Pei Yaojing, courtesy name Huanzhi, was the second son of Prefect of Ningzhou Shouzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yaojing, styled Huanzhi, was the second son of Shouzhen, prefect of Ningzhou.

sentences.zh: 數歲能屬文，擢童子舉，稍遷秘書省正字、相王府典簽，與掾丘悅、文學韋利器更直，備顧問，府中號「學直」。

translations.literal: At several years of age he could compose prose; he was selected on the Youth Examination, and gradually rose to Proofreader in the Secretariat and Record Keeper of the Prince of Xiang's household; together with aide Qiu Yue and literary adviser Wei Liqi he rotated night duty, standing ready for consultation, and within the princely household they were called the "Study Duty."
translations.idiomatic: While still a child he could write prose; selected on the Youth Examination, he gradually rose to proofreader in the Secretariat and record keeper in the Prince of Xiang's household. He rotated night duty with aide Qiu Yue and literary adviser Wei Liqi, standing ready to answer questions, and the household called them the "Study Duty."

sentences.zh: 王即帝位，授國子主簿，累遷長安令。

translations.literal: When the Prince took the imperial throne, [Pei] was appointed Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Education; through successive promotions he became magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince ascended the throne, Pei was appointed chief clerk of the Directorate of Education; through successive promotions he became magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 舊有配戶和市法，人厭苦，耀卿一切責豪門坐賈，豫給以直，絕僦欺之敝。

translations.literal: There was an old system of assigned households and market purchase; the people resented its hardship; Yaojing altogether assigned responsibility to great houses and seated merchants, pre-paying them the proper price, cutting off the abuse of rental fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system of assigned households and compulsory market purchase, the people suffered greatly; Yaojing made the great houses and seated merchants bear the burden, paid them the full price in advance, and put an end to the abuses of rental fraud.

sentences.zh: 及去，人思之。

translations.literal: When he departed, the people missed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office, the people longed for his return.

sentences.zh: 為濟州刺史，濟當走集，地廣而戶寡。

translations.literal: As prefect of Jizhou—Ji lay at a crossroads, the land broad but households few.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Jizhou, he governed a region at a major crossroads, broad in territory but sparse in population.

sentences.zh: 會天子東巡，耀卿置三梁十驛，科斂均省，為東州知頓最。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven toured east, Yaojing established three beam bridges and ten post stations, levies balanced and reduced, and ranked first among eastern prefectures in provisioning the imperial halt.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor toured east, Yaojing built three beam bridges and ten courier stations, kept levies balanced and light, and ranked first among the eastern prefectures in provisioning the imperial halt.

sentences.zh: 封禪還，次宋州，宴從官，帝歡甚，謂張說曰：「前日出使巡天下，觀風俗，察吏善惡，不得實。

translations.literal: Returning from the Feng and Shan sacrifices, the court halted at Songzhou and feasted the accompanying officials; the Emperor was greatly pleased and said to Zhang Yue: "Earlier, when I sent envoys to tour the empire, observe customs, and inspect the good and bad in officials, I did not get the truth.
translations.idiomatic: On the return from the Feng and Shan sacrifices the court stopped at Songzhou and feasted the accompanying officials; the Emperor was in high spirits and said to Zhang Yue, "When I earlier sent envoys to tour the realm, observe customs, and inspect officials' conduct, I did not learn the truth.

sentences.zh: 今朕有事岱宗，而懷州刺史王丘餼牽外無它獻，我知其不市恩也；

translations.literal: Now that I have gone to Mount Tai on state business, Prefect Wang Qiu of Huaizhou presented only a tethering horse and nothing else beyond it—I know he is not buying favor;
translations.idiomatic: Now, as I perform the rites at Mount Tai, Prefect Wang Qiu of Huaizhou has offered only a tethering horse and nothing more—I know he is not currying favor;

sentences.zh: 魏州刺史崔沔遣使供帳，不施錦繡，示我以儉，此可以觀政也；

translations.literal: Prefect Cui Yong of Weizhou sent envoys to supply provisions without using brocade or embroidery, showing me his frugality—by this one may observe his governance;
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cui Yong of Weizhou sent envoys to supply provisions without brocade or embroidery, showing me his thrift—by this one can judge his administration;

sentences.zh: 濟州刺史裴耀卿上書數百言，至曰『人或重擾，則不足以告成』，朕置書座右以自戒，此其愛人也。」

translations.literal: Prefect Pei Yaojing of Jizhou submitted a memorial of several hundred words, saying at one point, 'If the people are repeatedly harassed, the rites cannot be successfully completed,' and I have placed that memorial by my seat as a warning to myself—this is love for the people."
translations.idiomatic: and Prefect Pei Yaojing of Jizhou submitted a memorial of several hundred words, saying at one point, 'If the people are repeatedly harassed, the rites cannot be successfully completed.' I have kept that memorial by my seat as a warning to myself—this is true care for the people."

sentences.zh: 俄徙宣州。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 前此大水，河防壞，諸州不敢擅興役。

translations.literal: Before this there had been great flooding; river defenses were ruined; the prefectures dared not on their own initiate corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier there had been severe flooding that destroyed the river defenses, and the prefectures dared not undertake repairs on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 耀卿曰：「非至公也。」

translations.literal: Yaojing said: "This is not utmost impartiality."
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing said, "That is not the conduct of utmost public-mindedness."

sentences.zh: 乃躬護作役，未訖，有詔徙官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally supervised the labor; before it was finished, an edict ordered him transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon personally supervised the work; before it was finished, an edict arrived ordering his transfer.

sentences.zh: 耀卿懼功不成，弗即宣，而撫巡飭厲愈急。

translations.literal: Yaojing feared the work would not be completed; he did not at once announce [the transfer], but in console and inspection pushed urgency all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing feared the project would fail; he did not announce the transfer at once, but redoubled his supervision and urging on the work.

sentences.zh: 堤成，發詔而去。

translations.literal: When the dike was complete, he issued the edict [of transfer] and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the dike was finished, he proclaimed the edict of transfer and departed.

sentences.zh: 濟人為立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Ji erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Ji raised a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 歷冀州，入拜戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He served [as prefect of] Jizhou, then entered [the capital] and was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Jizhou, then entered the capital and was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 開元二十年，副信安王祎討契丹，又持帛二十萬賜立功奚官，耀卿曰：「幣涉寇境，不可以不備。」

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, he served as deputy to Prince Xin'an Li Yi in campaigning against the Khitan; he also carried two hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward meritorious Xi officials. Yaojing said, "When currency crosses enemy territory, one cannot fail to take precautions."
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan, he accompanied Prince Xin'an Li Yi against the Khitan and also bore two hundred thousand bolts of silk to reward Xi officials who had distinguished themselves. Yaojing said, "When gifts of silk must pass through enemy country, one cannot afford to be unprepared."

sentences.zh: 乃令先與期，而分道賜之，一日畢。

translations.literal: He therefore had appointments made in advance, then distributed the rewards by separate routes, finishing in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged fixed times in advance, then distributed the rewards along separate routes and completed the whole affair in one day.

sentences.zh: 突厥、室韋果邀險來襲，耀卿已還。

translations.literal: The Turks and Shiwei did indeed lie in ambush at a defile to attack, but Yaojing had already returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks and Shiwei did in fact waylay him at a narrow pass, but Yaojing was already back.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，雨害稼，京師饑。

translations.literal: The next autumn, rains ruined the crops and the capital suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn, rain destroyed the harvest and famine struck the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝將幸東都，召問所以救人者。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to visit the Eastern Capital and summoned [Yaojing] to ask how the people might be saved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor planned to travel to the Eastern Capital and summoned Yaojing to ask what could be done to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 耀卿曰：「陛下既東巡，百司畢從，則太倉、三輔可遣重臣分道賑給，自東都益廣漕運，以實關輔，關輔既實，則乘輿西還，事蔑不濟。

translations.literal: Yaojing said, "Since Your Majesty will tour east, with all the bureaus accompanying you, the Great Granary and the Three Adjuncts can send senior ministers by separate routes to distribute relief; from the Eastern Capital increase grain transport by water to fill the passes around the capital—once those passes are filled, the imperial carriage can return west, and nothing will fail to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing said, "Since Your Majesty will tour east with the full bureaucracy in attendance, senior ministers can be sent from the Great Granary and the Three Adjuncts along separate routes to distribute relief. From the Eastern Capital, expand water transport to stock the capital region; once that region is supplied, the imperial carriage can return west and every part of the plan will succeed.

sentences.zh: 且國家大本在京師，但秦地狹，水旱易匱。

translations.literal: Moreover, the state's fundamental foundation lies in the capital, yet the Qin region is narrow and drought or flood easily bring shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the state's root lies in the capital, but the Qin lands are cramped and easily exhausted by drought or flood.

sentences.zh: 往貞觀、永徽時，祿稟者少，歲漕粟二十萬略足；

translations.literal: In former times under Zhenguan and Yonghui, those on salary rations were few, and two hundred thousand shi of grain transported yearly was roughly sufficient;
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, those drawing state rations were few, and two hundred thousand shi of grain shipped each year was nearly enough;

sentences.zh: 今用度浸廣，運數倍且不支，故數東幸，以就敖粟。

translations.literal: now expenditures have gradually broadened, transport at several times that amount still cannot suffice, hence the frequent eastern visits—to draw on the stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: now expenses have steadily grown, and even several times that volume of transport cannot meet them, which is why the court so often travels east to draw on stored grain.

sentences.zh: 為國大計，臣願廣陜運道，使京師常有三年食，雖水旱不足憂。

translations.literal: For the great plan of the state, your servant wishes to broaden the Shaan transport route, so the capital always has three years' food—in drought or flood there will be no need for worry.
translations.idiomatic: For the long-term good of the realm, I wish to expand the Shaan transport route so that the capital always holds three years' grain; then drought and flood would no longer be cause for alarm.

sentences.zh: 今天下輸丁約四百萬，使丁出百錢為陜、洛運費，又益半為營窖用，分納司農，河南、陜州。

translations.literal: Today registered tribute males number about four million; let each male pay one hundred coins for Shaan and Luoyang transport costs, and an additional half for building granary pits, paid separately to the Director of Granaries in Henan and Shaan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Registered tribute males today number about four million. Let each pay one hundred coins toward Shaan and Luoyang transport costs, and half again as much for building granary pits, remitted separately to the Director of Granaries in Henan and Shaan.

sentences.zh: 又令租米悉輸東都。

translations.literal: Also order that all rent grain be delivered entirely to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Also require that all rent grain be sent in full to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 從都至陜，河益湍沮，若廣漕路，變陸為水，所支尚贏萬計。

translations.literal: From the capital to Shaan, the river grows ever swifter and shallower; if the transport route is widened and land transport changed to water, the expenditure would still save tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: From the capital to Shaan the river grows swifter and shallower; if the transport route is widened and carriage hauls are replaced by water carriage, the savings would still run to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 且江南租船候水始進，吳工不便河漕，處處停留，易生隱盜。

translations.literal: Moreover, Jiangnan rent-boats wait for favorable water before advancing; Wu craftsmen are ill-suited to river transport—stopping everywhere, pilferage easily arises.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jiangnan rent-boats wait for the right water levels before moving; Wu boatmen are unused to river transport, linger at every stop, and theft easily follows.

sentences.zh: 請置倉河口，以納東租，然後官自顧載，分入河、洛。

translations.literal: I ask that granaries be established at the river mouth to receive eastern rent, then the government itself hire carriers to distribute into the Yellow and Luo [rivers].
translations.idiomatic: I ask that granaries be set up at the river mouth to receive eastern rent, after which the government itself should hire carriers and distribute the grain onto the Yellow and Luo routes.

sentences.zh: 度三門東西各築敖倉，自東至者，東倉受之；

translations.literal: At Sanmen Pass, build relief granaries east and west of each [gate]; those arriving from the east shall be received by the eastern granary;
translations.idiomatic: At Sanmen Pass, build relief granaries on the east and west of each gate; grain coming from the east should be received by the eastern granary;

sentences.zh: 三門迫險，則旁河鑿山，以開車道，運十數里，西倉受之。

translations.literal: Sanmen being narrow and perilous, then cut into the mountain beside the river to open a cart road, transport [grain] for a dozen or so li, and the western granary shall receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sanmen is cramped and dangerous, cut a road through the mountain beside the river, haul the grain by cart for a dozen or so li, and let the western granary take it in.

sentences.zh: 度宜徐運抵太原倉，趨河入渭，更無留阻，可減費鉅萬。」

translations.literal: Estimate [grain] may be slowly transported to the Taiyuan Granary, hurry down the river into the Wei—no further delay or obstruction—and costs may be reduced by immense tens of thousands."
translations.idiomatic: From there it can be moved at an easy pace to the Taiyuan Granary, then rushed downriver into the Wei with no further holdups, cutting costs by vast sums."

sentences.zh: 天子然其計，拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事，充轉運使。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven approved his plan, appointed him Vice Director of the Huangmen Department and Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and made him Commissioner for Transport.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved his plan, appointed him Vice Director of the Huangmen Department and Associate Chief Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and made him Commissioner for Transport.

sentences.zh: 於是置河陰、集津、三門倉，引天下租繇盟津溯河而西。

translations.literal: Thereupon granaries were established at Heyin, Jijin, and Sanmen, drawing the empire's rent and corvée grain from Mengjin upstream along the river westward.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries were then established at Heyin, Jijin, and Sanmen, and the empire's rent and corvée grain were brought from Mengjin up the river to the west.

sentences.zh: 三年積七百萬石，省運費三十萬緡。

translations.literal: In three years they accumulated seven million shi and saved three hundred thousand strings in transport costs.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years they stockpiled seven million shi and saved three hundred thousand strings in transport expenses.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「以此緡納於上，足以明功。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "If this money were presented to the throne, it would suffice to make one's merit manifest."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "If this money were turned over to the throne, it would be enough to make one's achievements plain."

sentences.zh: 答曰：「是謂以國財求寵，其可乎？」

translations.literal: He replied, "That would mean seeking favor with state wealth—how could that be permissible?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "That would be using the state's wealth to buy favor—how could that be right?"

sentences.zh: 敕吏為和市費。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the clerks to use it for market-purchase expenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the clerks to apply it to market-purchase expenses.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palace Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Counselor.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以尚書左丞相罷，封趙城侯。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was dismissed as Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was removed as Left Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 夷州刺史楊浚以贓抵死，有詔杖六十，流古州。

translations.literal: Yang Jun, prefect of Yizhou, faced death for embezzlement; an edict ordered sixty strokes of the cane and exile to Guzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, prefect of Yizhou, was liable to death for corruption; an edict commuted this to sixty strokes of the cane and exile to Guzhou.

sentences.zh: 耀卿上言：「刺史、縣令異諸吏，為人父母，風化所瞻。

translations.literal: Yaojing submitted a memorial: "Prefects and magistrates differ from other officials—they are fathers and mothers to the people, looked to for moral transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing submitted a memorial: "Prefects and magistrates are not like other officials; they are fathers and mothers to the people, and all look to them for moral guidance.

sentences.zh: 令使裸躬受笞，事太逼辱。

translations.literal: To make them bear their bodies naked and receive beating—the affair is too coercive and humiliating.
translations.idiomatic: To make them strip bare and take the cane is far too degrading.

sentences.zh: 法至死，則天下共之。

translations.literal: When the law reaches death, the whole realm shares in it.
translations.idiomatic: When the law calls for death, the whole realm shares in that judgment.

sentences.zh: 然一朝下吏，屈挫牽頓，民且哀憐，是忘免死之恩，而有傷心之痛，恐非崇守長、勸風俗意。

translations.literal: Yet once brought down as a subordinate official, bent low and dragged through disgrace, the people will pity them—forgetting the grace of commuted death while bearing heart-rending pain; I fear this is not the intent of honoring local chiefs and encouraging custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once reduced to the status of a subordinate and broken in public, the people will pity them—forgetting the grace of a commuted sentence while nursing a wound to the heart. I fear this is not what is meant by honoring local chiefs and encouraging good custom.

sentences.zh: 又雜犯抵死無杖刑，必三覆後決，今非時不覆，或夭其命，非所以寬宥之也。

translations.literal: Moreover, for miscellaneous offenses carrying death without caning, judgment must follow triple review—now without review at the wrong season, some lose their lives prematurely; this is not the means by which to show leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, for miscellaneous capital offenses where the cane is not applied, the law requires threefold review before execution. To proceed without review at the wrong season is to cut short some men's lives; that is not how clemency should work.

sentences.zh: 凡大暑決囚多死，秋冬乃有全者。

translations.literal: Generally, those executed in great heat mostly die; only in autumn and winter are some spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: As a rule, prisoners executed in the height of summer mostly die; only in autumn and winter do some survive.

sentences.zh: 請今貸死決杖，會盛夏生長時並停，則有再生之實。」

translations.literal: I ask that commutations of death to cane sentences now coincide with the summer growing season and all be suspended—then there will be real opportunity for renewed life."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that all commutations from death to cane sentences be halted during the summer growing season, so that men may truly have a chance to live again."

sentences.zh: 是時，特進蓋嘉運破突騎施還，詔為河西、隴右節度使，因令經略吐藩。

translations.literal: At this time, Special Advancement Holder Gai Jiayun returned after defeating the Turgesh; an edict made him military governor of Hexi and Longyou, and ordered him to manage the Tibetan frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Gai Jiayun, holder of Special Advancement, returned after defeating the Turgesh; an edict appointed him military governor of Hexi and Longyou and charged him with managing the Tibetan frontier.

sentences.zh: 嘉運以新立功，日酣遨未赴屯。

translations.literal: Jiayun, fresh from victory, daily indulged in revelry and had not yet gone to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh from his victory, Jiayun spent his days in feasting and pleasure and had not yet reported to his post.

sentences.zh: 耀卿言於帝曰：「嘉運精勁勇烈誠有餘，然臣見其誇言驕色，竊憂之，恐不足與立事。

translations.literal: Yaojing said to the Emperor, "Jiayun truly has more than enough vigor and fierce courage—but I see boastful words and a proud bearing, and I secretly worry he may not suffice for accomplishing great affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing said to the Emperor, "Jiayun is indeed full of spirit and fierce courage, but I have seen boastful talk and a proud look on his face, and I privately worry that he may not be equal to the task.

sentences.zh: 今盛秋防邊，日月已薄，當與軍中士卒相見。

translations.literal: Now in the height of autumn, border defense is urgent and the days grow short—he ought to meet face to face with the soldiers in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Now, at the height of autumn when the frontier must be defended, the days are already growing short, and he ought to go face his troops in camp.

sentences.zh: 若不素講，雖決在一時，恐非制勝萬全之義。

translations.literal: If there has been no prior understanding, though resolve may be decided in a moment, I fear that is not the principle of securing victory in complete safety.
translations.idiomatic: If he has not prepared them in advance, a sudden decision may win a moment's success, but I fear that is not the way to secure a fully reliable victory.

sentences.zh: 且兵未及訓，不能知法；

translations.literal: Moreover, troops not yet trained cannot know the laws;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, troops that have not been drilled cannot know the rules;

sentences.zh: 士未懷惠，不可共心。

translations.literal: soldiers not yet cherishing grace cannot share one heart.
translations.idiomatic: and soldiers who have not felt the general's kindness cannot give him their full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 使幸而有功，非師出以律之善。

translations.literal: Even if by luck there is achievement, that is not the excellence of marching forth under the laws of war.
translations.idiomatic: Even if fortune should bring success, that would not be the true merit of sending an army forth in accordance with law.

sentences.zh: 又萬人之命倚於將，示不得已，故鑿兇門而出。

translations.literal: Again, the lives of ten thousand men depend on the general—showing there is no choice, hence the Xiong Gate is opened when marching out.
translations.idiomatic: Again, ten thousand lives hang on the general; to show that there is no turning back, the Xiong Gate is broken open when the army marches out.

sentences.zh: 今酣呶朝夕，胖肆自安，非愛人憂國者，不可不察。

translations.literal: Now he revels morning and night, fat and at ease—one who does not love people or worry for the state cannot fail to observe this.
translations.idiomatic: Now he feasts and carouses from morning to night, plump and at ease—anyone who loves the people and cares for the state cannot fail to notice this.

sentences.zh: 茍不易帥，宜嚴詔申約，以督其行。」

translations.literal: If he is not replaced as commander, a stern edict should renew the injunction to urge his departure."
translations.idiomatic: If he is not replaced as commander, a stern edict should restate the order and press him to take the field."

sentences.zh: 帝乃促嘉運詣部，卒無功還。

translations.literal: The Emperor then pressed Jiayun to go to his post; in the end he returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then pressed Jiayun to report to his command; in the end he returned without accomplishing anything.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，進尚書左仆射，俄改右仆射，而李林甫代之。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao, he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; soon he was changed to Right Vice Director, and Li Linfu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianbao he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; soon he was shifted to Right Vice Director, and Li Linfu took his place.

sentences.zh: 上日，林甫到本省，具朝服劍佩，博士導，郎官唱案。

translations.literal: On his first day, Linfu arrived at his department, fully dressed in court robes with sword and girdle ornaments, led by academicians while secretaries announced the cases.
translations.idiomatic: On his first day in office, Linfu came to his department in full court dress with sword and girdle ornaments, guided by academicians while secretaries called out the docket.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，就耀卿聽事，乃常服，以贊者主事導唱。

translations.literal: When the ceremony was complete, [Linfu] went to Yaojing's office of audience; [Yaojing wore] ordinary dress, with chief clerks as ushers leading and announcing.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony was finished, Linfu went to Yaojing's office; Yaojing wore ordinary dress and had chief clerks serve as ushers to lead and announce.

sentences.zh: 林甫驚曰：「班爵與公同，而禮數異，何也？」」

translations.literal: Lin Fu said in alarm, "Our rank and title are the same as yours, yet the ceremonial forms differ—why?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fu said in surprise, "Our rank is the same as yours, yet the ceremonial forms differ—why is that?"

sentences.zh: 耀卿曰：「比苦眩，不堪重衣。

translations.literal: Yaojing said, "Lately I have suffered dizzy spells and cannot bear heavy robes.
translations.idiomatic: Yaojing said, "Lately I have been troubled by dizziness and cannot endure heavy robes.

sentences.zh: 又郎、博士紛泊，非病士所宜。」

translations.literal: And the secretaries and academicians bustle about—inappropriate for one in ill health."
translations.idiomatic: And the secretaries and academicians bustle about—hardly fitting for a man in poor health."

sentences.zh: 林甫默然慚。

translations.literal: Lin Fu fell silent, ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Fu said nothing, ashamed.

sentences.zh: 居一歲，卒，年六十三，贈太子太傅，謚曰文獻。

translations.literal: After one year in office he died, aged sixty-three; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, posthumous name Wenxian (Learned and Presented).
translations.idiomatic: After a year in office he died at sixty-three; he was posthumously made Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, with the posthumous name Wenxian (Learned and Presented).

sentences.zh: 子綜，吏部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Zong was a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zong served as a bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 綜子佶。

translations.literal: Zong's son was Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Zong's son was Ji.

sentences.zh: 佶字弘正，幼能文。

translations.literal: Ji, style name Hongzheng, could compose prose while still young.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Hongzheng, could write prose even as a child.

sentences.zh: 第進士，補校書郎，判等高，授藍田尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, judged equal in rank, and was given the post of Blue Field district defender.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed collator, received an equal-rank evaluation, and was made defender of Lantian district.

sentences.zh: 德宗詔發畿縣民城奉天，嚴郢為京兆，政刻急，本曹尉韋重規妻乳且疾，不敢免。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong ordered men from the capital counties levied to fortify Fengtian; Yan Ying was metropolitan governor, his administration harsh and urgent; Wei Chonggui, defender of the original bureau, had a wife nursing and ill and dared not seek exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong ordered men from the capital counties levied to fortify Fengtian. Yan Ying was metropolitan governor, and his rule was harsh and pressing. Wei Chonggui, defender of the original bureau, had a wife who was nursing and ill and dared not ask to be excused.

sentences.zh: 佶請代役，要如程，當時稱其義。

translations.literal: Ji volunteered to serve in his place, fulfilling the quota as required; contemporaries praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Ji volunteered to take his place on the labor roster and met the quota as required; people at the time praised his sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 帝幸梁，佶奔見行在，授補闕。

translations.literal: When the Emperor went to Liang, Ji hurried to the mobile court and was appointed Remonstrance and Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor went to Liang, Ji rushed to the mobile court and was appointed Remonstrance and Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 李懷光以河中叛，佶建議請討，帝深器之。

translations.literal: Li Huaiguang rebelled from Hezhong; Ji proposed requesting a campaign against him, and the Emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huaiguang rebelled at Hezhong, Ji proposed that he be put down by force, and the Emperor came to think highly of him.

sentences.zh: 詔用盧杞為饒州刺史，與諫官執不可。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Lu Qi prefect of Raozhou; together with the remonstrance officials he held firm that this could not be.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Lu Qi prefect of Raozhou; Ji joined the remonstrance officials in insisting that this could not stand.

sentences.zh: 歷遷諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Remonstrance and Discussion Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 黔中觀察使。

translations.literal: [He became] observation commissioner of Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He became observation commissioner of Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 韋士文為夷獠所逐，詔佶代之，部夷安服。

translations.literal: Wei Shiwen was driven out by the Yi barbarians; an edict made Ji replace him, and the tribes of the command pacified and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shiwen was driven out by the Yi tribes; an edict made Ji replace him, and the tribes of the region settled down and submitted.

sentences.zh: 歷同州刺史、中書舍人，遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He served successively as prefect of Tongzhou and Secretariat Drafting Attendant, then was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as prefect of Tongzhou and Secretariat Drafting Attendant, then was promoted to Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時李巽以兵部尚書領鹽鐵，將遷使局就本曹，經構已半，會佶至，以為不可。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xun, as Minister of War, also headed the Salt and Iron Commission; he planned to move the commission's office into his own ministry, and construction was already half done—when Ji arrived, he judged it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Xun, as Minister of War, also headed the Salt and Iron Commission and planned to move the commission's offices into his own ministry; construction was already half finished when Ji arrived and objected that this could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 巽雖怙恩而強，猶撤之，時重其有守。

translations.literal: Though Xun relied on favor and was forceful, he still dismantled it; contemporaries respected Ji for his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xun relied on imperial favor and was forceful by nature, he still tore the work down; people at the time respected Ji for standing firm.

sentences.zh: 改吏部侍郎，以疾為國子祭酒、工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; because of illness he became Chancellor of the National University and Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel; because of illness he was made Chancellor of the National University and Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He died, was posthumously made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, posthumous name Zhen (Upright).
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, with the posthumous name Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 佶清勁明銳，所與友皆第一流，鄭餘慶尤厚善。

translations.literal: Ji was clear, vigorous, sharp, and discerning; those he befriended were all of the first rank, and Zheng Yuqing was especially close.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was upright, forceful, sharp, and clear-minded; those he befriended were all men of the first rank, and Zheng Yuqing was especially close to him.

sentences.zh: 既歿，餘慶為行服，士林美之。

translations.literal: After his death, Yuqing wore mourning garments for him—the literati praised this.
translations.idiomatic: After Ji died, Yuqing wore mourning for him as for a close friend, and the literati praised this.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：開元之盛，所置輔佐，皆得賢才，不者若張、源等，猶惓事職，其建明有足稱道。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In the splendor of Kaiyuan, the assistants appointed all obtained worthy talent; even those not so, such as Zhang and Yuan, still devoted themselves to duty—their constructive proposals merit mention.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In the glory of Kaiyuan, the ministers appointed were for the most part men of talent; even those who fell short, such as Zhang and Yuan, still devoted themselves to their offices, and their constructive proposals deserve to be remembered.

sentences.zh: 朝多君子，信太平基歟！

translations.literal: The court had many gentlemen—surely this was the foundation of great peace!
translations.idiomatic: The court abounded in gentlemen of worth—surely this was the foundation of an age of peace!

sentences.zh: 張氏三世宰相，然器有所窮，嘉貞窮於俗，延賞窮於忮，弘靖窮於權，惜哉！

translations.literal: The Zhang clan produced chancellors for three generations, yet each man's capacity had its limit—Jiazhen was limited by vulgarity, Yanshang by jealousy, Hongjing by power—alas!
translations.idiomatic: The Zhang clan held the chancellorship for three generations, yet each man's character had its limit: Jiazhen was cramped by vulgar ambition, Yanshang by jealousy, Hongjing by hunger for power—alas!
